01

Foundations.

For designers, developers, and junior teammates

Logo, color, typography, voice, imagery, shapes, the atoms that everything else is built from. Read this chapter first; every page, every component, every social post assumes you know these.

The Ghar.tv Wordmark
Full Wordmark Primary logo. Used wherever space allows the full brand name.
G Symbol, The Mark Standalone mark. App icons, favicons, social avatars, watermarks.
Real Estate. For You.
Mark + Tagline Compact lockup for stationery, event badges, social bios.
Copy the logo

The wordmark and the G mark, as copy-ready SVG. Copy puts the markup on your clipboard, SVG saves a file, and PNG renders a transparent raster at 1024px on the long edge, in whichever colour is selected.

Both files are self-contained: xmlns is present and no font, image or external reference is used, so they open in any editor and convert anywhere. The logo is never redrawn, re-spaced or recoloured beyond the three values here.

Three colours, and no fourth

Brand red #ee324b on light ground, white on a dark or photographic ground, ink #1a1714 where red would compete with the content beside it. The logo is never tinted to a theme colour, never gradient filled, never outlined, and never paired with a shape glyph.

DESIGN EXPLORATION
Imagery

Photography.
Warm, real, uncluttered.

Natural light. Indian or relatable Asian faces. Real interiors and architecture. Photos lead without overlays, the image is the story. Shapes and the G mark are used on photography only in print, merchandise, and editorial contexts.

Hero 4: 3
Discovery 1: 1
Editorial 4: 5
Shapes as decorative elements on photography, print, merch, social
G mark as subtle watermark on editorial photography
Photography Direction
Warm, natural light. Indian or relatable Asian faces when human subjects appear. Real interiors, real architecture, no stock-generic. Property photos use 4:3 aspect; heroes use 16:9; discovery grids use 1:1. When Pexels cannot provide confirmed Indian faces, use no-face alternatives: property aerials, city skylines, material close-ups.
Ghar Shape Library

Nine canonical silhouettes that anchor the Ghar.tv visual identity. Same wall stance (x=24 → 176), same baseline (y=170), same soft 28-unit rounded edge. Variations come from roof silhouette and colorway. Every shape is a clean filled vessel, usable as a mask, image holder, icon backdrop, or shape-as-card.

Nine shapes. One family.

Each shape is a variation on the fundamental "ghar", home. Different roof silhouettes, different colorways, one consistent family rendering rule. Together they form a visual vocabulary that's instantly recognizable and endlessly adaptable.

The G symbol is the primary brand mark. These nine shapes are a supportive visual vocabulary, decorative, versatile, never competing with the logo.

  2. 2Peak-leftTurmeric
  3. 3Peak-rightSand
  4. 4ManorTerracotta

Rule, inline in display type (baseline-grounded)

A canonical shape set inside a display headline is typography, not decoration, a noun standing in the sentence. Use a canonical path + its canonical colour only (clean filled vessel, never the billboard door/window variant). It must sit on the text baseline, grounded like a house on the ground, never vertically centred or floating. Size it ~1.05–1.1em (a touch taller than the caps), then nudge it down slightly so it settles into the line instead of towering. With two or more shapes, spread them apart, a different x-position on each line; never stack them at the same x on adjacent lines.

.headline      { line-height: 1.3 }              /* room so a raised glyph clears the line above */
.headline .t-line { display: block; white-space: nowrap }
.q-shape {
  display: inline-block; width: 1.08em; height: 1.08em;
  vertical-align: baseline;        /* sit ON the baseline (Clickl-style) */
  position: relative; top: .12em;  /* nudge down so it's grounded, not towering */
}
Copy the shapes

The nine silhouettes above, as copy-ready SVG. Paste one straight into a page and it renders with no build step, no sprite sheet and no dependency.

Copy puts the markup on your clipboard. SVG saves it as a file. PNG renders a transparent 1024 square in the colour this card is named for. The snippets carry no colour of their own: currentColor means a shape takes the color of whatever you put it inside, so one snippet serves every palette entry.

The family rule, why every shape carries a stroke

Eight of the nine draw a hard-cornered polygon, then round it by painting a 28-unit stroke in the same colour as the fill, with stroke-linejoin="round". The stroke is not an outline, it is the soft edge, and it expands the silhouette past the path, which is why the geometry stops at y=170 but the shape sits on y=184. Fill and stroke are both currentColor, so one color value drives the pair and they can never drift apart. If you replace them with literal hex values, they must match exactly or the edge will fringe.

Chimney Cottage (6) is the exception. Its curves are baked into the path, so it carries no stroke and needs none.

Recolouring is allowed and is how a shape adapts to a section; the nine colourways above are the defaults, not a lock. The geometry is not, do not re-point a path to make a “new” shape. Nine is the whole family. See the usage rules above for masks, icon backdrops and inline-in-headline placement.

Image Masks

Photos in
house shapes.

The signature technique, real photography masked into the nine canonical house shapes. Each silhouette creates a different visual personality while maintaining brand consistency. All paths byte-identical to the Ghar Shape Library above.

Living Space
Architecture
Interiors
Heritage
Saltbox
Cottage
Hillside
Modern
Design
⚠
These cannot be exported to PNG A masked photo is two things: the shape, which lives in the markup, and the photograph, which lives at a URL. When an SVG is loaded as an image (which is what SVGOMG, a PNG converter and every "save as image" button do underneath) the browser runs it in a mode that fetches nothing at all, so the photo never arrives and you get an empty shape or an outright failure. A local path does not help; the block is on loading anything, not on the domain.

Two ways through. To ship a masked photo on a page, use the markup exactly as it is here, since a live page loads the image normally. To ship one as a flat file, composite it in an image editor and export a PNG, or embed the photograph in the SVG as a data: URI, which makes the file self-contained but very large.

The nine plain shapes in 9 Canonical Shapes have no such limit: they reference nothing, so their Copy, SVG and PNG buttons all work.

House-masked photography on solid theme color backgrounds. Use for property cards, social media posts, event collateral, and editorial features. Each card pairs one shape with one color, text can sit inside the image with a gradient, or outside on the color surface.

Brand Voice

How Ghar.tv
sounds.

Intelligent, empowering, editorial. Written for the person visiting, not describing the business. Every line should feel like it respects the reader's time and intelligence.

Intelligent Empowering Trustworthy Editorial Premium Understanding-first

Do, Write Like This

Understand the market before you move. Empowers. Puts the reader in control.
India's most engaged real estate audience. Confident positioning without superlatives.
Build authority in your micro-market. Speaks to the broker's ambition, not our product features.
Homes worth talking about. Editorial. Evocative. Invites curiosity.
Conversations. One-word power. The GharTalks tagline says everything.

Don't, Never Write Like This

Find your dream home today! Salesy. Every portal says this. Zero differentiation.
We are India's #1 real estate platform. Unsubstantiated claim. Arrogant, not confident.
Get 500+ leads per month with our tools! Lead-gen language. Ghar.tv is understanding-first.
Like [other brand] but for Indian real estate. Reference brands are internal only. Never in user-facing copy.
Visit ghar.tv/intelligence for more. Raw URLs as copy. Use smart, human CTAs instead.

every size.

From a 16px favicon to a 200px billboard. Below 32px, use the G mark only. At medium sizes, mark or full wordmark. At large sizes, always prefer the full wordmark.

Restraint

Shapes support.
They don't dominate.

The nine shapes are a vocabulary, not a wallpaper. Use them at roughly 5% of any page view, one per section, never all at once. Ghar.tv must look diverse, not monolithic.

Avoid, Overloaded

Homes worth talking about.

When shapes appear in every heading, every card, every corner, the brand becomes monotone. The shapes lose their power and the platform stops looking diverse.

Preferred, Restrained

Homes worth talking about.

One shape per section. Let whitespace, typography, and photography do the heavy lifting. The shape becomes a punctuation mark, not the sentence.

01
The 5% Rule
Shapes occupy roughly 5% of any given page view, the same discipline as brand red. They accent, not dominate.
02
One Per Section
A section can have one inline shape, OR a masked photo, OR an accent mark. Never all three. Pick the single most impactful use.
03
Diversity Over Identity
Ghar.tv must look like a diverse platform, not "the shapes brand." Content, typography, and photography carry the identity, shapes support it.
02

Composition Rules.

For developers and page builders

Five non-negotiable rules every new page inherits, grid, section heads, the one CTA pattern, CTA placement, logo discipline. Foundations are the atoms; these are the load-bearing decisions that hold any page coherent.

Rule 01 · Container

The grid scales
with the screen.

One token, smooth across all viewports. The laptop floor stays calm; bigger monitors widen proportionally; the cap holds so 4K screens never become a billboard. Every section wrapper uses max-width: var(--max-w); margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 var(--pad-h), never invent custom widths.

/* :root */
--max-w: clamp(1280px, 75vw, 1840px);
--pad-h: clamp(24px, 3vw, 64px);
--pad-v: clamp(80px, 9vw, 120px);

Rule 02 · Section Head

Every section
opens the same way.

Eyebrow on its own row at the top, then a 2-column row at desktop: title on the left, lead + CTA stacked on the right. Below 1024 it stacks vertically. The reading rhythm is identical across Intelligence, Editorial, GharTalks, Voices, that's the point. Every section uses the shared .sec-head / .sec-eyebrow / .sec-title / .sec-lead classes; section prefixes only layer max-width overrides on top.

Section · Eyebrow

A short, rhythmic title that owns its line.

Lead paragraph, one or two sentences that set up the section. Kept under ~420px on desktop so it doesn't sprawl. Inter 15px, 1.75 line-height, espresso ink.

Section CTA 
<!-- Section markup pattern -->
<section id="intelligence">
  <div class="section-inner">
    <div class="sec-head">
      <span class="sec-eyebrow">Intelligence</span>
      <div class="sec-head-row">
        <div class="sec-head-l">
          <h2 class="sec-title">Markets, made readable.</h2>
        </div>
        <div class="sec-head-r">
          <p class="sec-lead">…</p>
          <a class="btn-text">Explore Intelligence →</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <!-- section content below -->
  </div>
</section>
Rule 03 · CTA Tiers

Two CTA tiers.
One per role.

Every CTA on the site belongs to one of two tiers, and they don't swap. Section main CTA is a bordered pill (.btn-text), used once per section, next to the lead or under the description. Card-internal CTA is a text+arrow link (.btn-link), used inside cards as a navigation cue because the card itself is already a click target. Putting a pill inside a card competes with the section CTA; putting a text link as the section CTA fails to anchor the section. One tier per role, never both.

Section · default Explore Services .btn-text, bordered pill, 1.5px ink border, 13/24 padding
Section · hover Explore Services Fills ink, arrow slides 3px right
Card · default Explore finance .btn-link, 13px ink, no border, no background
Card · hover Explore finance Color → brand-red, gap widens 6→9px, arrow slides 2px

Rejected variants, do not reintroduce

  • Pill on a card · competes with the section CTA. Cards are already click targets, use .btn-link for the inner cue.
  • Text link as section CTA · loses anchor weight. Section CTA needs the pill border to read as the section's primary call to act.
  • Filled brand-red buttons · red is reserved for page-level CTAs (Post Property, primary nav action) only.
  • Ghost / muted variants · both tiers stay ink-colored. No "Watch on YouTube" red, no muted-grey CTAs.
  • Custom paddings / sizes per section · tiers are canonical, .btn-text is 13/24, .btn-link is 13px text + 12px svg. No per-section tuning.
Rule 04 · CTA Placement

CTA goes under
the description.

Title + lead set the case for action. The CTA sits right there, readers don't need to scroll past arrows or dots to act. Foot rows stay reserved for arrows, dots, peek controls; never the section CTA.

✕ CTA in the foot row

Reader has to scroll past the carousel to act, and arrows + CTA compete for attention in the same row.

Rule 05 · Logo Discipline

The logo stands
alone, always.

A strict, non-negotiable rule. The Ghar.tv logo (the full red wordmark, the G letterform, or the mark + Suiza tagline lockup) is never paired with a shape glyph. The brand name “Ghar.tv” in a logo unit is never typed in Gazpacho, Inter, or any other font, it must use the canonical SVG logo asset. Gazpacho is fine when “Ghar.tv” appears inside a sentence or display title; it is not fine as a wordmark.

✕
Ghar.tv
House-shape glyph + Gazpacho text

Pairs a generic house glyph with a Gazpacho-rendered brand name. Neither piece is the actual logo. This pattern keeps appearing in footers, brand bars, and toast notifications, strip it on sight.

✕
Real logo + decorative shape glyph

Even when the actual logo is used, a shape glyph next to it is wrong. The logo carries its own identity. A shape next to it competes for the same job and reads as a second mark.

✓
Full Ghar.tv wordmark, the canonical logo

The real wordmark SVG. Use this in footers, navbars, and any moment that needs the full brand. Never replace the “Ghar.tv” characters with text styled in Gazpacho or Inter.

✓
G letterform, the standalone mark

Use the G letterform on its own when the full wordmark won't fit: app icons, favicons, social avatars, watermarks, copyright lines, notification toast icons. Never inside a colored badge or rounded square that mimics a logo lockup.

✓
A home worth talking about, that's what Ghar.tv is for.
“Ghar.tv” inside a sentence or title

When “Ghar.tv” appears inside running editorial copy, headlines, or display titles, it follows the surrounding font like any other word. Gazpacho is fine here, it's a sentence, not a logo unit.

Rule 06 · Whole-Card Link

The whole card
is the link.

When a card has one primary destination, wrap the entire card in <a> so the full surface is clickable. The "Explore X →" cue at the bottom stays for affordance but becomes a <span>, nested anchors are invalid HTML. Card hover propagates to the inner cue so the link visual updates from anywhere on the surface.

✓ Card is the anchor; inner cue is a span

Entire surface is the click target. The bottom “Explore X →” reads as a link cue, not a separate link.

<!-- The whole card is one anchor. -->
<a href="/services/finance" class="sv4-card sv4-card--finance">
  <div class="sv4-card-ico">…</div>
  <h3 class="sv4-card-name">Ghar Finance</h3>
  <p  class="sv4-card-desc">…</p>
  <!-- inner cue is a span, NOT an a -->
  <span class="btn-link sv4-card-cta">Explore finance →</span>
</a>
✗ Card is article, inner CTA is the anchor

Only the small “Explore X” text is clickable. Users who tap the card surface, image, or title get no response.

<!-- Click area limited to the inner text link. -->
<article class="sv4-card">
  <div class="sv4-card-ico">…</div>
  <h3 class="sv4-card-name">Ghar Finance</h3>
  <p  class="sv4-card-desc">…</p>
  <a href="/services/finance" class="btn-link">Explore →</a>
</article>

Required when the whole card is a link

  • Reset anchor styles on the card: text-decoration: none; color: inherit;
  • Focus-visible outline so keyboard users see card focus: outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 4px;
  • Propagate card hover to inner cue so the link visual reads from anywhere on the surface: .xx-card:hover .xx-card-cta { gap: 9px; } and .xx-card:hover .xx-card-cta svg { transform: translateX(2px); }, color stays ink, the hover cue is motion only (no brand-red flip on text links)
  • Inner cue is .btn-link per Rule 03, text+arrow, no border, because the card itself carries the click affordance
Rule 07 · Carousel Furniture

Furniture appears
only in carousel mode.

The carousel chassis (.rail-outer / .rail + initCarousel) is shared across every rail-using section. But the visible furniture, arrow buttons, cursor: grab, bleed-edge margins, appears ONLY at the breakpoint where the row overflows. On the grid breakpoint where cards fit, the chassis is silent. Disabled arrows on a grid that doesn't scroll read as broken UX. A grab cursor on a static row is misleading.

≥ 1024 px Grid mode · silent chassis

All 3 cards fit. No arrows, no bleed, no grab cursor.

Card 1
Card 2
Card 3
‹ ›
cursor: default
< 1024 px Carousel mode · furniture on

Track bleeds to viewport edges; next card peeks in the bleed zone. Arrows + grab cursor + drag are live.

Card 1
Card 2
Card 3
‹ ›
cursor: grab · margin: 0 calc(-1 * var(--pad-h)) · overflow-x: clip

Rejected variants, do not reintroduce

  • Arrows always visible (disabled on desktop) · reads as broken UX. If there's nothing to navigate, don't show the control.
  • Grab cursor on a non-overflowing grid · the cursor promises drag; the grid can't deliver. Misleading.
  • Bleed-edge margins on a grid layout · bleed exists so the next card peeks past the viewport edge. With no overflow, the “peek” never appears, just an awkward left/right gap.
  • Separate “always rail” chassis to dodge the rule · some sections naturally always overflow (Architecture & Design has 7 cards). That's the same rule applied to a section permanently in carousel mode, not an exception.
03

UI Components.

For developers

Buttons, inputs, dropdowns, modals, toasts, tabs, tooltips, navbars, pagination. Airbnb skeleton, Clickl soul. Every component lives here so future pages reach for the existing one rather than inventing a new variant.

Chapter 03 · Module 01

Buttons.

Two button worlds coexist on Ghar.tv. Editorial sections lean on a single text-link CTA and never break that rule. Transactional UI, search submit, sign-in, modal confirm, icon controls, navigation, uses the families below. This page is the canonical spec for every interactive button across the portal.

Editorial · Storytelling

Section CTAs.

Header CTAs, card CTAs, inline actions inside marketing & storytelling sections, Intelligence, Editorial, GharTalks, Voices, Architecture & Design, VideoWorks, Services, GharEvents, For Brokers, For Developers.

Two tiers, never mixed. Section main CTA = .btn-text, a 10px rounded outlined button (Family 02). Card-internal CTA = .btn-link, text + arrow, no border (Family 06). The pill is the section's voice; the link is the card’s.
See Rule 03, CTA Tiers
Transactional · Product UI

UI buttons.

Form submits (Sign In, Post Property, Subscribe), search submit, modal confirm/cancel, icon actions (close, profile, back), nav controls.

Reach for the families below. Primary, Secondary, Icon, Ghost. Each has defined sizes & states.
Browse the families

The most prominent action on a screen. Brand-red fill, white text. Use sparingly, one primary action per view, never two competing. Examples in production: Search submit in the universal search bar, Sign In in the auth modal, Post Property form submit, Subscribe in the footer card.

/* styles4.css */
.btn-text {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 13px 24px;
  background: transparent;
  border: 1.5px solid var(--ink);
  border-radius: 10px;        /* NOT 999px, that's the pill family */
  font: 600 13px/1 'Inter', sans-serif;
  letter-spacing: .01em;
  color: var(--ink);
  text-decoration: none;
  transition: background .22s ease, color .22s ease, border-color .22s ease, transform .22s ease;
}
.btn-text:hover { background: var(--ink); color: #fff; }
.btn-text:hover svg { transform: translateX(2px); }

A fully-rounded pill (999px radius), quieter than primary but still high-confidence. Ink border, transparent fill, fills with ink on hover. Use for transactional UI where a pill silhouette is right: the Post Property mark in the navbar, Cancel + Confirm pairs in modals, secondary CTAs paired with a primary. NOT for editorial section CTAs, that’s Family 02’s job.

06

Card link.

The card-internal CTA tier, a text + arrow link with no border, no fill. .btn-link on the homepage. Used as the sub-action inside an already-clickable card (e.g. Explore finance → inside a Ghar Finance service card, VideoWorks → inside the cinematic title-card hero). Inter 13–14 / 600, ink → brand-red on hover, arrow slides 2px right. Card hover propagates to this CTA via .xx-card:hover .xx-card-cta so the whole card surface lights it up. Never use as a section main CTA, that’s Family 02 (the rounded outlined pill).

In production: .btn-link · every whole-card-linked card on the homepage

Pair, don’t mix. Card link is the sub-action inside a card; Section CTA (Family 02) is the section’s main action. Putting .btn-link as the section CTA, or a pill as a card’s inner cue, breaks the visual tier. The full placement spec lives in Rule 03. Full spec

Red stays disciplined: only .arrow-link and modal legal links use it, everything else is ink or faint.

03 · Section wrap

Section wrap.

Every section on every page is centred at max-width: var(--max-w) (1280px floor, scales up on large displays) with horizontal padding from --pad-h. Before this, ~40 different per-section classes reimplemented the same three lines. Now: .section-wrap. Add as a co-class on the section element; the prefix class (.cl-section, .ep-section, etc.) only carries the section-specific top/bottom margin or background tint.

Default.

<section class="section-wrap my-section">
  <!-- content -->
</section>

/* And in CSS, keep the prefix class for unique top/bottom margin: */
.my-section { margin: clamp(96px, 10vw, 140px) auto 0; }

What you get from .section-wrap:

  • max-width: var(--max-w), 1280px floor, scales to 1840px on 2560px+ displays per [[feedback_container_width]]
  • margin-left/right: auto, centres in the page
  • padding-left/right: var(--pad-h), responsive horizontal padding (clamp 24px → 80px)

Bleed variant.

Use for: hero billboards / full-bleed image sections that need to ignore horizontal padding. Add the .section-wrap--bleed modifier.

<section class="section-wrap section-wrap--bleed">
  <!-- children can touch viewport edges -->
</section>

What collapsed into this: design.html, .cl-section, .nr-section, .ep-section ×5, .ad-around, .arch-layout, .guide-cards (all migrated 2026-06-09). index.html, .intl4-section, .ad4-section, .gt4-section, .vc4-section, .ge4-section, .fb4-section, .dm4-section, .vw4-section, .cn4-section, .sv4-section, etc. (pending, rename-only, behaviour-preserving per catalog constraint).

Now it's one: .sec-head + .sec-eyebrow + .sec-title + .section-head__link (all in styles.css).

Main.

Use for: top-of-section headers, Collections, Inspiration, Editorial. Gazpacho display title with an Inter tracked-caps eyebrow above and a text+arrow "See all" link on the right.

03 · Grid · 3-col editorial

3-col editorial grid.

Three columns, supporting left, prominent centre, supporting right. The centre column gets divider borders on desktop and a wider grid ratio. On mobile, columns stack in source order (default) OR centre-first (Hero pattern). Replaces .hero-v2__split and .nr-grid, both used the same pattern under different names.

Default.

Use for: editorial sections like Inspiration where the natural top-to-bottom column order is fine on mobile.

L · supporting
L · supporting
CENTRE · prominent
CENTRE · prominent
R · supporting
R · supporting
<div class="grid-3col-editorial">
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col">
    <!-- left supporting cards -->
  </div>
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col grid-3col-editorial__col--center">
    <!-- centre prominent cards -->
  </div>
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col">
    <!-- right supporting cards -->
  </div>
</div>

Breakpoints (from styles.css):

  • Mobile (default): single column, 48px row gap
  • ≥1080px: 1fr 1.6fr 1fr, 24px gap, centre col gets 1px divider borders L/R
  • ≥1280px: 1fr 2fr 1fr, centre column even more prominent

Centre-first.

Use for: hero layouts where the centre column carries the title/CTA and must appear FIRST when the layout stacks on mobile, even though it's middle in DOM order. Add the .grid-3col-editorial--center-first modifier.

<div class="grid-3col-editorial grid-3col-editorial--center-first">
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col">L cards (order 2 on mobile)</div>
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col grid-3col-editorial__col--center">
    Centre title (order 1 on mobile, middle on desktop)
  </div>
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col">R cards (order 3 on mobile)</div>
</div>

What collapsed into this: design.html .nr-grid + .nr-col + .nr-col--center (Inspiration, migrated 2026-06-09). design.html .hero-v2__split + .hero-v2__col-l/c/r currently uses the canonical chassis via co-class (full hero migration deferred, content-styling rules deeply reference .hero-v2__col-l, requires careful rewrite).

03 · Carousels

Carousels.

Two canonical variants. Every horizontal rail on the portal must use one of these, same class names, same JS, same responsive logic. Pages that invent new prefixes (cl-rail, ep-designers-outer, gt4-rail) drift the system; this catalog is the source of truth.

How it works: all chassis CSS lives in styles.css (lines ~3500–4100), driven by .rail-outer + .rail co-classes and variant modifiers. The JS is the single initCarousel() in ghar-carousel.js (window.initCarousel). Pages link both and call initCarousel({outer, track, ...}) with one canonical option set. Touch detection happens once at page load via an inline IIFE setting window.__GHAR_IS_TOUCH__; on real touch devices initCarousel adds .is-native and the rail switches to native scroll automatically.

Tag carousel.

Use for: chip/pill rails, Browse-by-City on the homepage, Collections on /design, any horizontal row of small chips with an icon + label (+ optional meta line). Mid-line hover arrows on desktop ≥1080px. Right-fade signals "more to scroll". Drag on desktop, native finger-scroll on touch.

Mumbai Celebrity Homes 24 homes Heritage Sustainable 31 stories Small Spaces Award Winners 14 projects First Home

Canonical HTML, copy-paste verbatim. Replace the chip content for your data; never change the wrapper class names.

<div class="rail-outer dc-track-outer" id="myRail">
  <div class="rail dc-track dc-cities-track" id="myRailTrack" role="list">
    <a href="/path" class="dc-city" role="listitem">
      <span class="dc-city-icon" aria-hidden="true"><svg ...></svg></span>
      <span class="dc-city-label">Single line chip</span>
    </a>

    <!-- 2-line variant (label + meta), add the .dc-city--meta modifier -->
    <a href="/path" class="dc-city dc-city--meta" role="listitem">
      <span class="dc-city-icon" aria-hidden="true"><svg ...></svg></span>
      <span class="dc-city-text">
        <span class="dc-city-label">Chip name</span>
        <span class="dc-city-meta">24 items</span>
      </span>
    </a>
  </div>
  <span class="dc-fade dc-fade--l" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="dc-fade dc-fade--r" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <button type="button" class="dc-arrow dc-arrow--prev" id="myArrowPrev" aria-label="Scroll left">...</button>
  <button type="button" class="dc-arrow dc-arrow--next" id="myArrowNext" aria-label="Scroll right">...</button>
</div>

Canonical JS init. Page must load ghar-carousel.js before this script.

(function init(){
  if (typeof initCarousel !== 'function') { setTimeout(init, 50); return; }
  var outer = document.getElementById('myRail');
  var track = document.getElementById('myRailTrack');
  initCarousel({
    outer: outer,
    track: track,
    arrowPrev: document.getElementById('myArrowPrev'),
    arrowNext: document.getElementById('myArrowNext'),
    fadeL: outer.querySelector('.dc-fade--l'),
    fadeR: outer.querySelector('.dc-fade--r'),
    snap: 'free',
  });
})();

Responsive behavior (handled by the chassis, do not reimplement): arrows only render on desktop ≥1080px; on hover the outer fades them in. On touch devices, initCarousel adds .is-native and arrows/fades vanish via the html.touch-device rule in styles.css; native finger-scroll + momentum take over. Bleed-edge margin matches --pad-h so the first chip aligns with the section content edge.

Card carousel.

Use for: large editorial / portrait / project cards, Featured Projects on the homepage, Designers on /design, anywhere a row of substantial cards needs paged navigation. Centered paginator below the rail (not in-rail arrows). Fractional --n peek on narrow viewports for "more →" affordance. JS sizes cards to fit; you only set the --n curve.

Canonical HTML. The .dc-block .dc-block--projects wrapper controls --n (cards visible) and --gap.

<div class="dc-block dc-block--projects">
  <!-- Optional: head with eyebrow + title + see-all -->
  <div class="dc-head">
    <span class="dc-eyebrow">Section eyebrow</span>
    <button class="btn-text">See all →</button>
  </div>

  <!-- The rail (chassis comes from styles.css) -->
  <div class="rail-outer dc-track-outer" id="myCards">
    <div class="rail dc-track dc-projects-track" id="myCardsTrack" role="list">
      <a class="dc-proj" role="listitem">...your card markup...</a>
      <a class="dc-proj" role="listitem">...</a>
      <!-- For portrait cards (.hr-card) instead of .dc-proj:
           use class="hr-card", JS still sizes them via widthMode:'fractional-n'.
           Add flex-shrink:0; min-width:0 to your card in CSS. -->
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Paginator, canonical centered prev/next below the rail -->
  <div class="dc-paginator">
    <button type="button" class="dc-page-btn" id="myCardsPrev" aria-label="Previous" disabled>...</button>
    <button type="button" class="dc-page-btn" id="myCardsNext" aria-label="Next">...</button>
  </div>
</div>

Canonical JS init.

(function init(){
  if (typeof initCarousel !== 'function') { setTimeout(init, 50); return; }
  var outer = document.getElementById('myCards');
  var track = document.getElementById('myCardsTrack');
  initCarousel({
    outer: outer,
    track: track,
    prevBtn: document.getElementById('myCardsPrev'),
    nextBtn: document.getElementById('myCardsNext'),
    snap: 'page',                  // arrow steps page-by-page
    widthMode: 'fractional-n',     // JS sizes cards to fit --n per breakpoint
    cssVarHost: outer,
    nVar: '--n',
  });
})();

For a custom --n curve (e.g. Designers wants 3 / 2 / 1.2 instead of Projects' 3 / 2.5 / 2 / 1.5 / 1), add a co-class to the dc-block wrapper and override:

/* In styles.css or page-scoped <style> */
.dc-block--designers { --n: 3; --gap: 24px; }
@media (max-width: 899px) { .dc-block--designers { --n: 2; } }
@media (max-width: 599px) { .dc-block--designers { --n: 1.2; --gap: 16px; } }

Responsive behavior: fractional --n (e.g. 1.2) automatically toggles .is-peeking on the outer, which bleeds the rail to viewport edges so the next card peeks past section padding. On touch devices, initCarousel flips to native scroll mode (.is-native) and the paginator hides via the html.touch-device rule. Touch users get native momentum + scroll-snap.

Brand ticker.

Use for: infinite-loop logo strips, Brands in Design directory, future "Customers" / "As seen in" / "Press" rails on any vertical landing. Continuous drift at ~0.5px/frame with seamless wrap, drag-to-pause with momentum release, IntersectionObserver-gated so it only ticks when on-screen. Different chassis from tag/card carousels: this one NEVER snaps and NEVER stops, just drifts.

Canonical HTML. Duplicate every item, Set 1 + Set 2, so the wrap is invisible.

<div class="ticker-outer ep-brands--ticker">  <!-- or your own prefix -->
  <div class="ep-ticker-track">
    <!-- Set 1 (visible) -->
    <a class="ep-brand">...logo + name...</a>
    <a class="ep-brand">...</a>
    <!-- Set 2 (duplicate of Set 1 for seamless wrap) -->
    <a class="ep-brand">...same as first item in Set 1...</a>
    <a class="ep-brand">...</a>
  </div>
</div>

Canonical JS init. Page must load ghar-ticker.js before this script.

<script src="ghar-ticker.js" defer></script>
<script defer>
  (function init(){
    if (typeof initTicker !== 'function') { setTimeout(init, 50); return; }
    var outer = document.querySelector('.ep-brands--ticker');
    if (!outer) return;
    initTicker({
      outer: outer,
      track: outer.querySelector('.ep-ticker-track'),
      itemSelector: '.ep-brand',
    });
  })();
</script>

Optional opts: speed (px/frame, default 0.5), cooldownMs (drag cooldown, default 1500), momentumMul (velocity multiplier for drag-release glide, default 220), glideDur (release animation seconds, default 0.45). halfWidth measurement is derived from Set2[0].offsetLeft - Set1[0].offsetLeft so the wrap teleports between visually-identical positions (no jump). Outer needs overflow-x:clip + soft mask-fades on L/R for the cleanest look, see .ep-brands--ticker in styles.css for reference.

Future variants.

  • Photo essay, single-pane snap carousel for large image panels (Spaces section). Already uses initCarousel({snap:'card', widthMode:'fractional-n'}), document here.
  • Editorial card rail, variant of card carousel for 4:3 editorial cards (used on /design Editorial section). Could reuse card carousel with a different gap + aspect override.
04 · Cards

Cards.

Canonical card chassis + the reusable sub-components that live inside cards (feature lists, video play overlays, hover utilities). Every new section that needs a card MUST start from one of these, never a fresh prefix. See styles.css for the chassis rules.

Editorial / portrait card · .hr-card

Use for: 4:5 image-fill hero / editorial / portrait cards used across /design hero rows, designers carousel, brand spotlight, and Industry Voices. Standard hover-zoom (scale 1.04 / 1.05 via consolidated rule). Whole-card anchor link. Optional overlay text, dek reveal on hover, eyebrow chip. Variants: .hr-card--ed (editorial), .hr-card--lead (16:10), .hr-card--wide (16:10).

Canonical HTML, copy-paste verbatim.

<a class="hr-card hr-card--ed" href="/path/to/story">
  <div class="hr-card__thumb">
    <img class="hr-card__media" src="..." alt="">
  </div>
  <span class="hr-card__eyebrow">Section · Sub-tag</span>
  <h3 class="hr-card__title">The headline goes here</h3>
  <div class="hr-card__dek-wrap">
    <p class="hr-card__dek">Dek paragraph revealed on card hover.</p>
  </div>
</a>

Responsive + interaction: chassis is whole-card anchor per feedback_whole_card_link. Image-zoom on parent hover (scale 1.04) comes from the consolidated rule at the top of design.html style block, do not re-author per section. Dek reveal uses grid-template-rows:0fr → 1fr transition. Touch devices skip hover (tap → navigate).

Card hover lift · .card-hover-lift

Use for: any whole-card link that should have the standard 3px upward lift + soft shadow + border-darken on hover. Used by GharTalks, GharEvents, and General Events cards on the homepage. Just add the class as a co-class on your card wrapper.

Canonical HTML.

<a class="my-section-card card-hover-lift" href="/path">
  ...card content...
</a>

Animates: transform: translateY(-3px) + layered shadow + border-color darken. Pairs with .btn-link CTA inside the card, both respond to the card-level :hover. Never add transition-all; the chassis uses targeted transitions.

Video thumbnail play overlay · .thumb-play

Use for: any card whose thumbnail represents a video, GharTalks episode cards, Architecture & Design home-tour cards, VideoWorks reel slots. Wrapper centres a glassmorphic play circle (.thumb-play-btn) over the image. Hover scale + darken comes from the parent card's :hover.

Canonical HTML.

<div class="thumb-wrap">            <!-- your card image container -->
  <img src="thumb.jpg" alt="">
  <div class="thumb-play" aria-hidden="true">
    <span class="thumb-play-btn">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="M8 5v14l11-7z"/></svg>
    </span>
  </div>
</div>

Behavior: thumb-play wrapper uses position:absolute; inset:0; pointer-events:none so it never steals clicks from the parent anchor. The button is a styled glass pill (white blur + ink play icon). Parent :hover nudges scale on the button via styles.css, never reimplement.

Feature list · .feat-list

Use for: small "what's included" capability lists inside cards, 3 to 6 rows of icon + title + 1-line description. Currently used by the SuperPro card (For Brokers) and Mandate card (For Developers). Anything that needs a "feature row" pattern should reach for this, never invent a per-section prefix.

Sample product

Lead paragraph explaining what this product does, in one sentence.

  • First capability Short description that fits on one line.
  • Second capability Each row independently aligned to a 22px icon column.
  • Third capability Top hairline rule + 16px gap between rows.

Canonical HTML, copy-paste verbatim. Icon column is fixed 22px; SVG inside takes .svg-fill.

<ul class="feat-list">
  <li class="feat-list__item">
    <span class="feat-list__icon" aria-hidden="true">
      <svg class="svg-fill" viewBox="0 0 24 24" ...>...</svg>
    </span>
    <span class="feat-list__text">
      <span class="feat-list__title">Row title</span>
      <span class="feat-list__desc">One-line description.</span>
    </span>
  </li>
  ...repeat li for each row...
</ul>

Mobile note: on phones the feat-list is typically hidden via a per-section rule (.your-section .feat-list { display:none }) because the card is a directional gateway, the full list lives on the linked destination page. Choose per section.

05 · Section block

Section block.

The OUTER wrapper that gives a section its vertical rhythm + optional background tint. Pairs with .section-wrap (the inner content centering chassis). Together they handle every section's outer shell, never author padding: var(--pad-v) 0 manually per section.

Default · .section-block

Use for: any section that needs the standard top/bottom vertical padding (var(--pad-v) = clamp 80px / 9vw / 120px). Replaces 11+ per-section duplicates like .gt4 { padding: var(--pad-v) 0 }.

<section id="my-section" class="section-block my-section">
  <div class="section-wrap my-section-inner">
    ...content...
  </div>
</section>

Warm-white tint · .section-block--warm

Use for: sections that need a warm off-white band (Editorial, Services, VideoWorks on the homepage). Co-class onto .section-block.

<section id="my-section" class="section-block section-block--warm">
  <div class="section-wrap">
    ...content...
  </div>
</section>

Pills strip · .section-pills-strip

Use for: the row of category pills/chips between a section head and the carousel below it. This is the role-named spacing class, replaces per-section drift like .intl4-chips-outer (32→44 clamp), .ad4-pills-outer (28→40), .gev-chips-outer (28→40 + top margin). Standardized 2026-06-09 to margin-bottom: clamp(28px, 3vw, 40px). Add the optional --gap-top modifier when the strip also needs top breathing room.

<!-- Standard: pills strip below head, carousel below strip -->
<div class="rail-outer tag-strip-outer section-pills-strip">
  <nav class="rail tag-strip" aria-label="Section categories">
    <a href="..." class="tag-strip-item">...</a>
    ...
  </nav>
</div>

<!-- With top breathing room too -->
<div class="rail-outer tag-strip-outer section-pills-strip section-pills-strip--gap-top">
  ...
</div>

The principle (READ THIS): if a section needs spacing in a SLOT that already has a canonical class, pills-strip, section-head, section-block, feat-list, co-class it. NEVER create a new .X-pills-outer or .Y-chips-wrap or .Z-head { margin-bottom: 32px } just to set one margin. Per [[feedback_reuse_shared_classes]], a one-property class is the worst kind of drift, every section ends up with a slightly different clamp() value and the design loses rhythm. Tailwind reference: Tailwind handles this with utility classes like mb-8; we handle it with semantic role-named classes that bake in the standard value.

06 · Utilities

Utilities.

Single-declaration helper classes. Add the class as a co-class on any element that needs the behavior, never duplicate the body inline. Replaces ~15+ small dupes across index.html + design.html.

.svg-fill

Use for: any inline <svg> that should fill its containing box (icon container with explicit width/height). Body: display:block; width:100%; height:100%.

<span class="icon-box"><svg class="svg-fill" viewBox="...">...</svg></span>

.absolute-fill

Use for: any element that should fill its (positioned) containing block, backdrop shapes, decorative overlays, image-fill layers. Body: position:absolute; inset:0; width:100%; height:100%.

<div class="parent">     <!-- needs position:relative -->
  <span class="absolute-fill"><svg class="svg-fill">...</svg></span>
</div>

.img-cover

Use for: any <img> that should fill its parent with object-fit:cover. Body: display:block; width:100%; height:100%; object-fit:cover.

<div class="card-thumb"><img class="img-cover" src="..." alt=""></div>

Line clamp · .line-clamp-1/-2/-3/-4

Use for: backend-driven titles, deks, excerpts that should truncate at N lines instead of pushing the card to varying heights. Replaces 13+ inline copies of the same display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp; -webkit-box-orient:vertical; overflow:hidden boilerplate. Pairs with the dynamic-content flex rule per [[feedback_dynamic_content_flex]].

<h3 class="hr-card__title line-clamp-2">{{ backend.title }}</h3>
<p  class="hr-card__dek   line-clamp-3">{{ backend.excerpt }}</p>

Truncate · .truncate

Use for: single-line backend strings that must NOT wrap, chip labels, button text, city names. Body: overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap.

<span class="dc-city-label truncate">{{ backend.cityName }}</span>

Aspect ratio · .aspect-1-1/-3-2/-4-3/-4-5/-3-4/-16-9/-16-10/-21-9

Use for: WRAP every dynamic <img> in an aspect-locked container. The container holds the layout; the image cover-crops to fit. Backend image dimensions can vary wildly, these classes guarantee a consistent grid. Body: aspect-ratio: N/M + overflow:hidden; position:relative.

<div class="card-thumb aspect-4-3">
  <img class="img-cover" src="{{ backend.image }}" alt="" loading="lazy">
</div>

Tabular nums · .tabular-nums

Use for: any element rendering backend numbers (prices, stats, ratings, counts). Forces digit-width alignment so columns of numbers line up across rows. Body: font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums.

<span class="cn4-metric-v tabular-nums">₹{{ backend.value }}</span>

Empty collapse · .collapse-when-empty

Use for: any optional backend field that may render as empty string. Without it, an empty <span> still consumes a flex-gap and leaves orphan whitespace. With it, an empty element collapses (display:none). Also: .rail:empty, .dc-track:empty, .grid-3col-editorial:empty, .feat-list:empty, .dc-paginator:empty all auto-collapse via the canonical layer.

<span class="hr-card__eyebrow collapse-when-empty">{{ backend.eyebrow }}</span>
<p    class="hr-card__byline collapse-when-empty">{{ backend.byline }}</p>

Flex-shrink safe · .flex-shrink-safe

Use for: any flex child that holds backend text (titles, leads, body copy). Adds min-width: 0 so long strings don't push the flex parent. Already baked into .section-head__text, .hr-card__body, .feat-list__text; apply elsewhere as needed.

<div class="card-row">     <!-- display: flex -->
  <img class="img-cover aspect-1-1" src="..." alt="">
  <div class="flex-shrink-safe">
    <h3 class="line-clamp-2">{{ backend.title }}</h3>
  </div>
</div>

Color utilities · .text-* / .bg-* (Tailwind-style)

Use for: set color or background to a brand token DIRECTLY on the element, never via a parent-variant selector. Replaces 15+ per-section variant rules like .X-card--variant .X-icon { color: var(--TOKEN) }. Mirror of the Tailwind utility approach but using Ghar.tv brand tokens.

/* Text color (sets `color`) */
.text-terracotta   .text-turmeric   .text-indigo   .text-sage   .text-sand   .text-aubergine
.text-espresso     .text-ink        .text-muted

/* Background color (sets `background-color`) */
.bg-terracotta     .bg-turmeric     .bg-indigo     .bg-sage     .bg-sand     .bg-aubergine
<!-- BAD, per-variant CSS authored per section -->
<style> .X-card--tips .X-icon { color: var(--terracotta); } </style>
<div class="X-card X-card--tips"><svg class="X-icon">...</svg></div>

<!-- GOOD, utility class on the SVG, no per-variant CSS needed -->
<div class="X-card X-card--tips"><svg class="X-icon text-terracotta">...</svg></div>

Cascade note: these utilities live in styles.css early in the cascade. If your section's inline style block has a base rule like .X-icon { color: var(--default) }, that base rule will WIN because inline styles come later. Either remove the base default or route through the utility instead of a per-variant selector. Per [[feedback_no_spacing_only_class]] this applies to color/background drift, not just spacing.

07 · Hover micro-interactions

Hover micro-interactions.

Five canonical hover transforms. ALL card hover behavior on the portal must use one of these. Per-section variants are a duplication trap, the consolidated block at the top of design.html already handles every combination. When you add a new card, ADD ITS SELECTOR to the consolidated rule, never re-author the same body.

/* 1 · Standard image zoom, editorial card hover */
.X:hover .X-image,
.Y:hover .Y-image,
... { transform: scale(1.04); }

/* 2 · Bigger image zoom, lead-spread / hero feature */
.A:hover .A-image,
... { transform: scale(1.05); }

/* 3 · Small arrow shift, in-card CTA chip */
.B:hover .B-cta svg,
... { transform: translateX(3px); }

/* 4 · Medium arrow shift, section-level CTA */
.C:hover .C-cta svg,
... { transform: translateX(4px); }

/* 5 · Title darken, editorial card hover */
.D:hover .D-title,
... { color: var(--espresso); }

When adding a new card: append your selector to the matching rule at the top of design.html <style> block, DO NOT create a new .your-card:hover .your-thumb { transform: scale(1.04) } rule per section. That's the duplication pattern this catalog exists to prevent.

Chapter 03 · Inputs & Search

Search & inputs.

Search is the portal's front door, and it ships as one system with many surfaces, a full desktop bar, four collapsed triggers, a suggestion panel, a full-screen mobile modal, and a separate brand finder. All logic lives in main.js; the classes below are the contract. Wire new search entry points to these, never re-author a bar.

01

Search triggers.

Four collapsed entry points share one surface treatment (.search-trigger, white fill, rule border, soft double shadow, ink-border on hover). Each is a different structural element by ID; the class only paints the surface so they read as one family. Below 744 every trigger opens the same mobile modal.

Chapter 03 · Forms

Forms.

Every form on Ghar.tv is built from one family: .jm-* for controls and chrome, .brf-* for the row grid and form-level error. It already ships in three live modals, sign-in, brand contact, project brief, and it is what Post Property, Post Requirement and the SuperPro application will be built from. Read .jm- as “Ghar form”, not “join modal”. Controls below are live: type, tick, drag a file in.

01

One control class.

.jm-field paints text, email, tel, <select> and <textarea> identically: 1.5px rule border, 14px radius, ink border on focus. There is no separate select or textarea class, and adding one is how a fork starts. Forms are placeholder-driven by default, each control says what it is inside itself, and a select's first option is its label, carrying aria-label so screen readers get the same cue.

styles.css:1106 · .jm-field
Live · real classesType in them
+91
  • .brf-row puts two controls on one line as a 1fr 1fr grid and drops to a single column below 560px. It is the only layout class a form needs.
  • Selects use their first option as the label, so a disabled placeholder option carries the prompt and never submits a value.
<!-- Text, email, tel, select and textarea all take .jm-field -->
<input type="text" name="name" class="jm-field" placeholder="Your name" required>

<!-- Two controls on one line -->
<div class="brf-row">
  <select class="jm-field" aria-label="Which city?">
    <option value="" selected disabled>Which city?</option>
    …
  </select>
</div>
02

Labels, required, help text.

Short modals stay placeholder-driven. Long multi-section flows, Post Property, the SuperPro application, need a persistent label, because a placeholder disappears the moment you type and the user loses the thread halfway down a twenty-field form. The red asterisk is a functional signal that the field will block submit, so it sits inside the 5% red budget; the label itself never turns red.

  • Help explains; it never repeats the label. If the help text is just the label reworded, delete it.

03

Field states.

Four states beyond default: focus (ink border), error (red border plus a message), valid (--sage border, used only where confirmation genuinely helps, a verified phone), and disabled. Errors name what happened and how to fix it. They do not apologise and they are never vague.

styles.css · .is-error · .jm-field-err · gharFieldError()
Live · all four statesClick the button to toggle

Enter a 10 digit mobile number. This one has 5.

  • gharFieldError(field, message) is the one way to set or clear a field error. It moves the red border, the message and aria-invalid together, so none of the three is ever left behind. Pass null to clear.
  • .jm-field-err is the per-field message. .brf-error is the form-level summary above the submit button. Do not swap them.

04

Checkbox, radio, switch.

The native input stays in the DOM and is visually replaced, so keyboard, form submission and assistive tech all work without extra code. The distinction that matters: a checkbox commits on submit, a switch commits immediately. Use a switch only where flipping it takes effect there and then, like a notification preference. Radios are for one-of-few; past five options, use a select.

  • The whole <label> is the hit area, so the text is clickable, not just the box.

05

Chips & tiles.

A checkbox is right for a short list of words. It is wrong for a set the user is meant to scan and compare, amenities, property type, configuration, the whole filter sheet. There the option itself should be the target. .jm-chip is a pill for many short options; .jm-tile is a block for a few that need explaining. Both are still native inputs underneath: swap checkbox for radio and nothing else changes.

styles.css · .jm-chip · .jm-tile
Live · multi-select chipsCheckbox semantics · many can be on
  • The outline carries the state; the fill only supports it. A 2px ink outline plus a --warm-white fill. Four fills were tried before this one: a cold grey wash read as disabled, brand mist and rose read as a campaign page, a warm sand wash was barely a state at all, and solid ink broke on content.
  • Why solid ink was wrong, and this is the argument that settles it. These controls have to host third-party marks, “link your Square Yards profile”, a social platform picker, a partner selector. Plenty of those logos are solid black, and a black logo on an ink fill is invisible. A selection state that destroys the thing being selected is broken, not bold. Solid ink also forced secondary copy to translucent white, which is where an unreadable chip count came from.
  • The fill is a Foundation tone, not an ink alpha. An alpha grey sits on top of whatever is behind it and goes cold and dirty; --warm-white is the canvas the rest of the portal is built from, so a selected control reads as part of the page. Hover on a selected control changes no colour at all and lifts with a shadow only. Secondary copy darkens to --espresso when selected and never inverts.
  • The second border pixel is an inset box-shadow, not a border-width change. Growing 1px to 2px reflows every neighbour in the wrap row, and a row of chips visibly twitches as you select through it.
  • Chips clear 48px, well past the 44px touch minimum, and the row wraps rather than scrolling so nothing hides off-screen in a filter sheet.
Live · single-select chipsRadio semantics · exactly one
  • Same class, different input type. .jm-chip--sm is the dense variant for a filter sheet, where full-size chips would push the apply button below the fold. It still clears 40px.
  • A result count belongs in .jm-chip__count, muted so the label still leads. Never show a count of zero as a live option: disable it.
Live · tilesFor options that need explaining
  • The grid is auto-fit with a 260px floor, so two columns become one on a phone without a breakpoint and a long description never squeezes the column.
  • An unavailable option is disabled rather than removed. Hiding it makes the user wonder whether they missed it; disabling it answers the question.
Live · stacked, with tick badge.jm-tile--stack · .jm-tile__check
  • The tick badge is opt-in. The border carries the selected state on its own; add the badge only where the tile is picture-led and a border reads as decoration rather than as state.
Live · options carrying a logo.jm-chip__logo · .jm-tile__logo
  • The logo sits on its own white plate, never on the control. The selection fill can never land behind a mark, so a solid-black wordmark stays legible whether the option is selected, hovered or disabled. This is what ruled out a solid-ink selected state: it would have erased exactly these logos.
  • Same rule the brand pages already follow, a logo tile is white or dark to suit the mark, never the surface it happens to land on. Use .jm-chip__logo--dark for marks that are white-on-transparent.
  • When disabled, only the mark dims (opacity:.4). The plate keeps its white, because a greyed plate behind a greyed logo makes the brand unrecognisable rather than merely unavailable.
<label class="jm-chip">
  <input type="checkbox" name="platforms" value="anarock">
  <span class="jm-chip__logo"><img src="…/anarock.svg" alt=""></span>
  ANAROCK
</label>
State contractBoth chips and tiles
StateTreatmentWhy
Default1px --field-rule border, white fillReads as available, not as chosen. A light ink tone, not the sand --rule: a beige box reads as decoration, not as somewhere to act.
Hover--warm-white fill, rule to --field-rule-hover, soft liftWrapped in @media(hover:hover) so it never sticks on touch.
Focus-visible2px ink outline, offset:2pxSits outside the box, so it never hides the selected border underneath.
Selected--ink rule + inset 1px, --warm-white fill, ink textTwo pixels of outline with no reflow. The outline carries the state, so the fill can stay light enough for any logo to sit on it.
Selected + hoverNo colour change. Lifts with a shadow only.Every deeper fill tried here was a near-neutral grey (--bg3, ink alphas) and read as a smudge beside the warm surface. The outline already says selected, so hover only has to acknowledge the pointer. Restated rather than inherited so it cannot depend on which rule wins the cascade.
Activescale(.985)Press feedback on touch, where there is no hover to confirm the tap landed. Skipped under reduced motion and when disabled.
DisabledWarm grey fill, muted text, icon at 40%Visible but clearly out of reach. Disabled, never hidden.
  • Every state is driven by :has() on the real input, so there is no .is-selected class for JS to set and forget. Tick the input and the styling follows.

06

Either/or, and what pairs with it.

Chips are for a set you scan and compare. A question with two or three fixed answers, buy or rent, this property type or that, is not that set: the answers are known, short, and mutually exclusive, so the control should read as one switch rather than as several competing objects. .seg--choice is the segmented control's paint on radio semantics: a role="radiogroup" of role="radio" keyed off aria-checked, with the chosen surface as a single thumb that slides and resizes to whichever option is on, instead of blinking off in one place and on in another.

styles.css · .seg--choice · main.js · segThumb()
Live · click or use arrow keysRadio semantics · exactly one
  • Segments size to their own label. “Residential” and “Land” are not the same word and do not want the same box; forcing them equal leaves the short one swimming and the long one tight. flex:1 1 auto gives each a content-width basis and shares the remainder evenly, so the difference survives and the row still fits the card at 390 rather than scrolling its last option off the edge.
  • The slide is a clip-path inset on one full-width layer, not a moving box. Variable widths mean a translate alone cannot fit the thumb to its target, and animating the thumb's own width would lay out a box every frame. clip-path stays off the layout path the way transform does, and inset() carries its own round, so the end caps are redrawn at each size instead of being squashed by a scale.
  • The shadow is drop-shadow, not box-shadow, and that is load-bearing. clip-path would cut a box-shadow off at the clip edge; a filter is applied after the clip and traces the shape it actually produced.
  • Positions are measured in px from the OPTIONS, never from the group's scrollWidth. The thumb is absolutely positioned inside the group and so counts toward its scroll overflow: measure the group and the thumb's own width becomes the thing being measured, and the value can then only ever grow. A ResizeObserver and document.fonts.ready re-fit it when the container or the font changes, and mobOpenAcc() re-fits on expand, a group inside a collapsed section has no width to measure.
  • That observer watches the PARENT, and only reacts to a width change. Stacking makes the group taller, which makes its host taller: an observer on the group, or one that reacts to height, feeds itself. The row-or-column decision depends on available width alone, so height changes are noise.
  • Until that first measure the group has no [data-seg-ready]: the thumb stays clipped away, the chosen button paints its own static pill, and the transition is off. The control is readable with no JS and nothing animates in from the wrong place.
  • Semantics are radio, not tab. It reuses the .seg paint but not its meaning: a tablist swaps a panel, this one records an answer. The delegated listener in main.js drives both shapes off one select(), reading aria-checked here and aria-selected there.
  • Selecting fires a native change that bubbles, so whatever owns the answer hears it from the pointer and the keyboard alike. Wiring the setter to an inline onclick instead is how the arrow keys silently stop updating state.
  • The listener runs on capture. A choice group nested in a clickable row has to stop the click reaching that row, and a bubble-phase listener would then never see it at all.
  • When the labels cannot make one row, the control stacks. Not a wrap, which strands a lone segment on its own line and reads as a mistake, and not a scroll, because an option you have to swipe to reach is one most people never see. segFit() asks the question by dropping back to a row first, testing while already stacked always answers “fits”, and the control could never come back. Segments never shrink (flex:1 0 auto) so the overflow it measures is real rather than an artefact of squeezed labels.
  • Stacking is not a second code path for the thumb: it is clipped on all four sides, so a column is just a different set of numbers. The track drops from 999px to 22px + the gutter, since a pill only stays a pill while it is one row tall, and content goes left-aligned, centred labels down a column read as a row that got squeezed.
  • The gutter widens when stacked (--seg-pad 4px → 8px, row gap 5px). A column reads tighter than a row at the same value: side by side the space between two pills doubles as the space around them, while stacked there is a long straight edge down each side with nothing in it. It is a variable rather than a number because the thumb is positioned from it and segThumb() measures against it, hard-coding 4px in three places is how the thumb ends up 4px out the day the padding changes, so the JS reads the computed padding instead of assuming one.
  • Optional .seg__ico, the same idiom as .jm-chip__icon and .jm-tile__icon: a line drawing on currentColor, so it inverts with its label under the thumb and needs no separate rule for the ink variant. Silhouettes have to survive 17px, so each is two or three strokes. A first pass at Land drew a plot with a survey flag and read as a mushroom at that size; the folded map replaced it.
  • A selection animates; a re-measure lands. The layer's height is not a transitioned property, so on a re-fit it jumps while the clip insets are still interpolating, for a beat the thumb covers the whole stack before settling onto one row, which is what expanding a collapsed section used to look like. segThumb(list, false) sets [data-seg-jump] for the write, reads a layout property to commit it, then gives the transition back. Selections keep their slide.
  • Segments clear 44px. The slide is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion; the thumb still lands in the right place, it just does not travel.
  • Labels are the words the search is read in, not the ones the database stores. Residential / Commercial / Land sit over keys that stay homes / workspaces / land, because those map to propertytypeid. One TYPE_LABEL map owns the display strings, the ternary behind them was repeated in six places, where a rename meant six edits and any miss showed two names for one thing on a single screen.
Live · ink thumb.seg--ink
  • One extra class. Same markup, same thumb, same motion, only the thumb's fill and the chosen label's colour change, so there is no second control to keep in sync.
  • Use it when the answer is the heaviest thing on the surface and nothing beside it is filled: a standalone toggle in a settings row, a card whose only other action is a link. It states the answer more firmly, which is the point.
  • Do not use it beside a filled button. Two dark blocks in one view is the exact failure the light thumb was introduced to fix; if the surface also carries a commit, the light thumb is the right one and .btn-text is what sits next to it.
  • The label crossfades on the thumb's clock rather than the faster default, so white text never sits on the light track mid-slide.
Live · stackedSame markup, narrower box
  • Nothing here is set to stack. It is the identical group as above in a 260px box, and segFit() reached a different answer, widen the box and it returns to a row on its own.
  • Drag the browser across the threshold to watch it flip. The thumb re-fits from the same measurements either way, so there is no moment where it is sitting on the wrong option.
What pairs with itOne filled object per view
Buy or rent?
Choose how you’d like to search.
  • Ink means one thing per view. This card originally answered the question with a solid ink fill and advanced with a solid ink button. Two dark blocks, and the larger of the two was the answer, so the heaviest object on the card was not the thing to do next. The rule that falls out: a filled surface is the commit, and there is one of them.
  • Moving between steps is .btn-text, the outline action, unmistakably a button, but it does not spend the ink the commit needs. The commit here is the search modal's red Search, pinned in the footer and visible the whole time, which is exactly why Next cannot also be heavy.
  • This does not contradict chips & tiles, where a chosen chip is solid ink. A chip row is a set of small pills in a wrap, and the chosen one is one pill among many. A two-answer switch filling the card width is a slab, and a slab outranks everything beside it.
  • Past five answers this control is wrong and the answer is a select. Past three that need explaining, it is .jm-tile.
  • In production on the search modal's Mode and Type steps (partials/mobile-search-modal.html), which used to be two flex:1 buttons on a bespoke .mob-sel-btn with its own chosen and unchosen colours. That fork is gone, and the four #mobileModal rules that painted it went with it. Both steps run .seg--ink, which the card can carry because the only other action on it is an outline .btn-text, put a filled button back beside it and the light thumb is the one to use.
The view-switching sibling, Tabs · Segmented control

    Long-form structure.

    09

    Submit outcomes.

    A submitted brief replaces the form in place with a success panel. It is never a toast: a toast disappears in four seconds, and someone who just sent a project brief wants to know what happens next. Toasts are for actions that need no follow-up.

    Debt The family is named .jm-* after the join modal it was born in, but it is now the portal form system used by three unrelated modals. Renaming means touching three shipped partials plus main.js, so it stays and is documented here instead. .brf-row and .brf-error are the same story from the brief modal. Do not add a third prefix: extend .jm-*.

    Chapter 03 · Navigation

    Navbars.

    The portal ships one navigation system with defined variants. Chapter 04 · Patterns draws what each surface looks like (desktop bar, mobile bottom bar, off-canvas menu); this module is the functional contract, the classes, JS hooks, responsive tiers, and behaviors every page inherits. Reuse these verbatim; never fork a per-page navbar.

    01

    Universal navbar.

    A three-column CSS grid, 1fr auto 1fr: logo left, universal search centre, actions right, that morphs on scroll. Above the fold the search is a full expanded bar; past 8px it collapses into a compact pill so the row stays quiet while reading.

    Chapter 03 · Dropdowns

    Dropdowns.

    Three shapes, and the choice between them is about list length, not taste. A plain <select> handles anything under a dozen options and costs nothing. A popover handles a short list that needs richer rows than a select allows. A searchable panel is for lists nobody can scan, countries, cities, categories, where typing beats scrolling.

    01

    Native select.

    The default, and correct far more often than it gets used. select.jm-field adds exactly two things on top of the shared field box: the portal's own chevron, and a colour fix for the option list. It inherits mobile's native picker for free, which no custom panel can match.

    styles.css:6276 · select.jm-field

    02

    Searchable panel.

    The country-code picker in the auth flow, and the model for any list too long to scan. A trigger showing the current value, a panel with a filter input pinned at the top, and scrollable options below. CLAUDE.md is explicit that country code is a searchable dropdown of 20+ countries, never a toggle.

    Chapter 03 · Modals & Dialogs

    Modals & dialogs.

    A modal interrupts. Earn it: use one when the task genuinely cannot continue underneath, signing in, sending a brief, confirming something irreversible. Everything below rides one shell at four widths, and every modal becomes a full-screen sheet below 744px.

    01

    The shell.

    .jm-overlay plus .jm-modal and a size token. The shell owns positioning, the 20px radius, the scale-in entrance, the scroll container and the phone sheet. Content owns nothing but its own markup. Open and close by toggling .jm-open on both.

    • Focus returns to the trigger on close, so a keyboard user is not dropped at the top of the document.

    02

    Confirm dialog.

    Only for actions that cannot be undone. If the action is reversible, do it immediately and offer Undo in a toast instead, that respects the 90% of people who meant it. The destructive button carries the action's own verb, never “OK”, so the button and the question cannot drift apart. .jm-btn--danger is the one place a red fill is correct.

    styles.css · .jm-confirm · .jm-btn--danger
    Live · the dialog bodyShown inline here; normally in a .jm-size-sm modal
    Delete this listing?

    The 2 BHK in Bandra West goes offline immediately and its 14 saved enquiries are removed with it. This cannot be undone.

    • Name the consequence, not the mechanism. “Its 14 saved enquiries are removed with it” is what the user actually needs to weigh.
    • The safe choice sits left and the destructive one right, matching the actions row everywhere else, so muscle memory is not punished here of all places.
    Chapter 03 · Toasts & Notifications

    Toasts.

    A toast confirms something that succeeded and needs no follow-up: saved, copied, removed. If the user must read it, act on it, or would lose something by missing it, it is not a toast, it is a panel or a dialog. Everything here comes through gharToast(). Never hand-author toast markup.

    01

    Four variants.

    The surface stays ink on every variant and only the icon takes colour, so a stack of toasts reads as one system and none shouts louder than another. Each colour is a theme token chosen because it means that thing, never picked for variety: --sage reads as settled and done, --turmeric is the caution colour everywhere else on the portal, --indigo is the neutral informational tone. Error is the exception that earns --red, as a functional alert rather than decoration, and it also earns a left rule and no auto-dismiss. Sage and indigo are lifted toward white because they sit on an ink surface; the raw tokens are tuned for warm-white and go muddy on dark.

    main.js · gharToast() · styles.css · .toast
    Live · fires a real toastBottom right on desktop, bottom centre on mobile
    Success Info
    Warn Error
    With Undo Stacking
    OptionDefaultNotes
    type'success'success | info | warn | error
    bodyn/aSecond line, for detail the title cannot carry.
    duration4000 · 0 on error0 keeps it until dismissed.
    actionn/a{ label, onClick }. One action only, usually Undo.
    • Errors do not auto-dismiss. A message you are meant to act on should not vanish while you are still reading it.
    • The host is aria-live="polite" and lifts to assertive only while an error is showing, so a confirmation never interrupts a screen reader mid-sentence.
    • Copy goes in through textContent, not innerHTML: toast text can carry a property name or a locality the user typed, and neither is trusted markup.
    // Confirmation. Clears itself in four seconds.
gharToast('Property saved');

// Reversible action: do it, then offer the way back.
gharToast('Removed from saved', {
  action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore }
});

// Error. Persists until dismissed.
gharToast('Could not send your brief', {
  type: 'error', body: 'Check your connection and try again.'
});
    When a panel beats a toast, Forms · Submit outcomes
    Chapter 03 · Tabs & Pills

    Tabs & pills.

    Three row-of-options patterns already exist and they are not interchangeable. Tabs switch the view without leaving the page. Filter pills narrow a list that stays on screen. Subnav navigates between pages. Picking the wrong one tells the user the wrong thing about what their click will do.

    01

    Which one.

    Decide by what happens on click, not by how the row looks.

    ContractCanonical source

    Underline tabs.tabsSwaps a panel in place, wider row. Overview / Specs.

    Section subnav.subnavNavigates to another page.

    Segmented control.

    A compact pill group for two to five mutually exclusive views. Past five options the answer is a select. aria-selected is the single source of truth: the CSS keys off it, so there is no second .active class to drift out of sync.

    Chapter 03 · Tooltips

    Tooltips.

    A tooltip is the last resort, not the first. Put help in the interface itself wherever it fits, a clearer label, a line of .jm-help under the field. Reach for a tooltip only to gloss a term the reader may not know: carpet area, RERA ID, super built-up. Never hide anything required to finish a task inside one.

    01

    Inline gloss.

    CSS only, no JS. The trigger is a real <button>, so the bubble shows on :focus-visible as well as hover, touch devices cannot hover, and a hover-only tooltip is invisible on half the portal's traffic.

    styles.css · .tip · .tip__trigger · .tip__bubble
    Live · hover or Tab to itAbove by default
    In a label Carpet area The usable floor area inside your walls. Smaller than built-up, and much smaller than super built-up.
    In a stat ₹24,800 per sq ft Median of registered sale deeds in this locality over the last six months.
    Flipped below RERA registered Registered with the state Real Estate Regulatory Authority. Use .tip--below near the top of a viewport.
    • aria-describedby ties the trigger to the bubble, so the gloss is announced with the control rather than being decorative text a screen reader skips.
    • Keep a tooltip under about twenty-five words. Longer than that and it wants to be help text or a link.

    02

    Naming a control.

    When the thing that needs naming is the control, an icon button in a bar, a social mark, a logo with no room for a label beside it, there is nothing to hang a ? off. .tip__anchor adds no appearance at all: the control keeps every style it already has and gains the reveal. Use it instead of the hover-expand pill, where a control grows sideways to show its own label, that moves layout on hover, it opens in one direction only, and on touch it never opens.

    Chapter 03 · Pagination

    Pagination.

    For a paged result set: the brands directory, the people directory, pillar archives. Distinct from .dc-paginator, which is the carousel's dot row. Prefer load-more where the reader is grazing, and numbered pages where someone needs to get back to a known position.

    01

    Numbered pages.

    Use when position matters, a directory someone will come back to, or a result set worth linking. Numbers collapse on mobile, where prev, next and the count carry the load and a full number row would not fit a 390px screen anyway.

    styles.css · .pager · .pager__btn
    Live · click a pageResize to see the mobile collapse
    …

    Page 1 of 12 · 284 brands

    • Prev on page one is aria-disabled="true" rather than removed, so the row does not reflow and shift the next button under the cursor.
    • Numbers are tabular-nums, so the buttons keep their width as the digits change.
    • The count states the total. “Page 1 of 12” alone does not tell anyone whether it is worth paging on.
    02

    Load more.

    The default for editorial browsing, where the reader is grazing rather than looking for a known item. One button, the count beside it, and the next batch appends in place. Chosen over infinite scroll because infinite scroll makes a footer unreachable and takes the reader's sense of how much is left.

    Chapter 03 · Disclosure & Loading

    Accordion & skeleton.

    Two patterns the portal kept re-inventing per page. An accordion for content worth having but not worth showing at once, and a skeleton for the gap between a request and its answer.

    01

    Accordion.

    Native <details> and <summary>, so it works before JS lands and keyboard support costs nothing. For FAQs and long specs. Never hide primary content in one: if the page's job depends on it, it belongs open.

    styles.css · .acc · .acc__item
    Live · open themWorks with JS disabled
    What does Ghar.tv charge a buyer?
    Nothing. Browsing, saving and enquiring are free, and always will be. The platform is paid by developers, brands and brokers for marketing and media, never by the person looking for a home.
    Are the listings verified?
    Every listing carries who posted it and when it was last updated. Where a project is RERA registered, the number is shown and links to the state authority's own record, so you can check it rather than take our word for it.
    How is SuperPro different from a normal broker listing?
    SuperPro is invite-only and limited by location. It is a full digital presence rather than a directory entry: a branded page, video production, and placement across the editorial network. It is about authority in a market, not lead volume.
    • The plus turns to a minus by rotating one stroke and fading the other, so the state change is a movement rather than an icon swap.
    • Summary rows clear 44px, and the whole row is the hit area rather than the text alone.
    02

    Skeleton.

    Use only where the real layout is already known, so the skeleton matches the shape that lands. A skeleton that does not match its content is worse than a spinner: it promises the wrong thing and the correction reads as a glitch. The sweep stops entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

    styles.css · .skeleton
    Live · animatingCard skeleton beside the real card shape
    • Widths vary between lines. A block of identical bars reads as a pattern, not as text about to arrive.
    • .skeleton forces color:transparent, so it can be applied to an element that already holds its real text while that text loads.

    Delete this listing?

    04

    Patterns.

    For page builders

    Applied recipes from the homepage. Card families, hero, navigation, footer, B2B layouts, vocabulary you reach for when a future page needs the move. These exhibits are not mandatory checklists; the framework rules above (Composition Rules) are. Browse for inspiration; reuse what fits.

    01.
    Warm paper is the canvas.
    White is an object, not a surface.
    02.
    The house is a glyph.
    It lives inside sentences.
    03.
    Color is vocabulary.
    Each tone means something, or stays away.
    04.
    Stories, not specs.
    Every word chooses the reader.
    05.
    The product participates in the room.
    It never yanks you elsewhere.
    Voice, Billboard Quote

    A place you can truly call your ghar.

    Understanding real estate, so you don't have to guess. Discover properties, markets, and the people who shape them.

    Section rhythm

    Sixteen sections. One voice.
    Five earned tones. Eleven stay on paper.

    The homepage stays on warm paper. Five sections earn their own surface, drawn from India's earth, never a Western pastel. Indigo Mist for Editorial (the ink of written voice). Espresso for GharTalks (the warm dark of a listening room). Turmeric for GharEvents (ceremony, haldi, festival gold). Ink for VideoWorks (the deeper dark of a cinema). Terracotta for Community (the earth that holds people and brands together). No tone is used twice. No two colored sections sit side by side, every colored moment is earned, and every earned moment breathes.

    Warm paper
    Default canvas. Everything begins here.

    ecoForYou Four verticals, who is this platform for?
    Warm paper
    Cards carry the accent. The section stays calm.
