    03, Shape as glyph (use cases)

    A vocabulary,
    not a stamp.

    The shapes are a design vocabulary you can reach for sparingly, inside an editorial sentence, opening a quotation, framing a photo. They are not a category-marking system. Don't prefix every section's eyebrow, every card's tag, or every label with a shape, the page becomes a wallpaper. The exhibits below show valid moments; on production pages, expect to use one such moment per page at most.

    Exhibit A, Shape as noun
    Home is where Maya, her little son laughs, and the afternoon light settles on the wooden floor.
    The shape replaces the word. Three houses read as three rooms, three ways a home holds a moment. The eye doesn't trip, it glides through the sentence.
    Exhibit B, Shape as window
    A two-bedroom apartment in Bandra where the mornings smell of filter coffee, and the sea is eight minutes away on foot.
    The shape becomes a window. Photography fills the house-silhouette and lives mid-sentence. Listing copy becomes a short story.
    04, Card taxonomy

    One voice. Many cards.
    Generic types and section-specific designs.

First, the generic content-type cards, Property, Editorial, Podcast, Event, Person, Intelligence, share a single chassis and exist for any page that needs a content card without a section-specific design. Second, the five section-specific families from the homepage, each solves a distinct content problem with its own visual identity. Reach for the closest match; don't invent a new pattern.

    06, The rules for scaling the voice

    Eight principles.
    If a decision breaks any one of them, the decision is wrong.

    These aren't style guidelines. They're the rules that keep the voice coherent across sixteen sections, six card types, B2C and B2B audiences, and years of future content. When you're three screens deep into a layout decision and can't choose, come back here.

    01
    Warm paper is the canvas.
    Body is #faf7f2 everywhere, product surfaces too. Pure white is a deliberate object that floats on the paper (inner cards, search bars, pills). If a section needs pure white, it's wrong.
    02
    The house is a glyph.
    The nine canonical shapes are typography. They live inside sentences, prefix categories, open quotes, anchor data. Never decoration. Never icons. If a shape isn't doing the work of a letter, cut it.
    03
    Color is vocabulary, earned, not assigned.
    Indigo Mist for Editorial (written ink), Espresso for GharTalks (listening room), Turmeric for GharEvents (ceremony), Ink for VideoWorks (cinema), Terracotta for Community (earth of people). Five earned tones, none repeated, none adjacent. If you can't defend a color choice semantically in one sentence, and the section next to it isn't warm paper, it doesn't belong.
    04
    Stories, not specs.
    Write every line for the person reading, not the business speaking. "5 new listings match your filter" becomes "a new home story starts with five matches." This is not word-play, it's stance.
    05
    The product is a polite guest.
    Search bars sit next to fireplaces. Notifications speak softly. The interface participates in the room, it doesn't yank you out of it. If a component interrupts the mood, rewrite the component.
    06
    Data is typography.
    Big serif stats. Shape-silhouettes as data dots. Histograms, not rainbow pie charts. Intelligence without clinical. Assume the reader can read a chart, don't dumb the data down to marketing.
    07
    B2B earns authority through craft.
    Broker, developer, and partner sections keep the warm voice but swap emotion for precision. Sharper type hierarchy, tighter grids, denser proof. Never colder color, just tighter composition. Atmosphere stays; editorial shifts.
    08
    One voice. Sixteen rooms.
    Variety lives within the voice, not against it. Different sections have different weight, density, color, and rhythm, but the reader should never feel they left Ghar.tv. If a section feels like it belongs to a different brand, it does. Rebuild it.
    A homepage isn't a screen. It's an opening chapter.
    Build every section as if the reader will stop here and read to the end.
    Ghar.tv · Real Estate. For You.
    Welcome to Ghar.tv. Meet the brands and the people behind them.

    Two directories, not one destination. Brands is the companies: developers, material brands, PropTech, finance. People is the individuals: architects, designers, economists, founders. They are separate verticals on purpose, because a reader looking for a practice and a reader looking for a person are not doing the same thing.

    Browse brands Browse people
    07 · Navigation

    One mark, one contextual action,
    everything else in the menu.

    Shared chrome, generated from partials/nav.html and styled by nav.css. It is not one bar: a body class selects the variant, and the difference between them is deliberate. The homepage carries the property search because searching is why people arrive there. A content page does not, because it would compete with the thing the reader came to read, so that page trades the search for its vertical's name and one contextual CTA. The exhibits below are live iframes of real pages, so they cannot drift from what ships.

    Variant A · HomeNo body class · the search is the point of the page
    Live height 117px mark · search (city, mode, type, submit) · Post Property · account · menu
    Variant B · Content pagebody.simple-nav.content-nav.cta-brief
    Live height 81px mark + vertical name · Share a brief · menu. No search, no account icon
    Variant C · Phone390px · the bar moves to the bottom
    Live 390 × 844 · top bar plus the fixed bottom bar
    • The four-tab bottom bar is the primary navigation on a phone: Ghar, Post Property, Account, Menu. It is fixed, so it survives the whole scroll.
    • The top bar keeps the mark and the search trigger only. Everything else has already moved down.
    • Below 744px a page with its own second-level bar may hide the masthead on scroll. A page without one may not, because that leaves no chrome at all. The gate is window.gharCanCollapseNav().
    Choosing a variantBody classes, not forks
    Body classWhat it doesUsed by
    noneFull search bar in the nav, Post Property pill, account iconindex.html
    simple-navDrops the expanded search for a single trigger; kills the scroll animation; 80px barEvery inner page
    content-navShows the mark plus its vertical's name as a lockup/brands, /people, /design, /voices
    cta-briefReveals the Share a brief CTADirectory and profile pages
    cta-subscribeReveals the Subscribe CTAEditorial pages
    nav-searchReveals the icon-only search buttonPages with an in-page finder
    • Every control ships on every page and is switched on by a class. A control added to one page's markup is deleted by the next npm run build:partials, silently, because the build reports success either way.
    • Add the class and its handler together. A page carrying the class with no handler ships a dead button.
    • index.html is not on the partial system and keeps its own inline copy of the nav CSS. A portal-wide nav change has to be made in both places or the homepage quietly diverges.
    • nav.css is served raw with a ?v=N cache-buster on 17 pages. Bump it in the same commit as any change to it.

    09, Micro-UI

    Every tooltip is a sentence.
    Every toast, a tiny story.

    Micro-UI is where most products break character, the form error, the success toast, the empty state, the tooltip. On Ghar.tv, these speak in the same voice as the editorial: warm, human, specific. Never "Error 404" when we can say "we couldn't find that page, let's help you find one that fits."

    10, B2B layout options

    Authority without cold.
    Layouts to reach for when designing B2B sections, not a fixed pattern.

    B2B pages are where most warm-voice platforms crack and turn into SaaS dashboards. Grey panels. Blue CTAs. Stock icons. On Ghar.tv, the flex works differently: tighter hierarchy, denser proof, precise type, but the paper stays warm and the serif keeps reading. The card pattern below is one option for a B2B layout, useful when proof points need to stack in 3-column rules. Sections like For Brokers and For Developers should pick the composition that fits the offering, image-masked shape windows, editorial broadsheet spreads, asymmetric splits, single hero cards. Treat hp-b2b as a vocabulary, not a template.

    SuperPro · For brokers

    Own your market.
    Not a listing page.

    An invite-only platform for brokers who want to be the name people search for in their city. Branded digital HQ, cinematic video production, featured placement across Ghar.tv, everything that separates a real authority from a results row.

Other options are valid and often better: image-masked shape windows (For Developers v8), editorial broadsheet spreads with oversized numerals, asymmetric splits with a profile card and supporting panel (For Brokers), centered single composition.     Ghar.tv helps you discover not just properties, but the neighborhoods, the markets, and the people who make a place feel like home.

    05

    UX Principles.

    For product, design, and developers

    How interactions should feel, calm, mobile-first, intuitive, trustworthy. Touch targets, scroll behavior, overlays, loading states, errors, accessibility. The platform takes Airbnb as primary reference; storytelling sections layer in Apple / Squarespace / Linear / Stripe motion craft, never breaking the calm.

    01

    Four commitments

    What every screen owes the reader

    This chapter is the behaviour contract. Chapter 03 says what a component looks like; this says how it must behave once a real person, on a real phone, with a real connection, tries to use it. Each rule below was written after a specific bug, and the bug is named so nobody has to rediscover it.

    The fourIn priority order
    CommitmentWhat it means in practiceFails when
    CalmOne primary unit per section. Whitespace is structure, not leftover. Colour carries meaning, never variety.Four stacked features in one section, each with its own accent
    Legible on a phone firstEvery layout is designed at 390px and then given room, not designed wide and then squeezed.A desktop row that only wraps politely because today's data is short
    Honest about stateEmpty, loading, partial and error each have a designed answer. No spinner standing in for an empty result.A section head with a "See all" link above nothing
    ReachableKeyboard, screen reader, reduced motion, 44px touch targets, AA contrast. Not a pass at the end.Hover-only affordances and focus rings removed for looks
    Reference frameWhere each influence applies, and where it stops
    • Airbnb is the skeleton. Calm surfaces, modular cards, discovery-driven browsing, intuitive search. This governs the default state of every page.
    • Apple, Stripe, Linear, Squarespace are the storytelling layer. Scroll-driven reveals, typographic hierarchy, precision. They apply to specific homepage moments, never as a blanket theme.
    • Dark is a moment, not a mode. Any dark panel is deliberate and contained. The portal has no dark theme.
    • Reference brands are internal vocabulary. They never appear in user-facing copy.
    02

    Philosophy

    Understanding-first, not transaction-first

    Ghar.tv is not a listing portal. The reader arrives to understand a market, a building, a person or a decision. That single fact settles most interface arguments before they start.

    What follows from itDecisions this rule has already made
    • Editorial beats promotional. The first viewport of a content page carries content. No paid surface sits above the first editorial block, and none appears in the first viewport at all.
    • Section CTAs navigate, they do not convert. A homepage section CTA goes to that vertical's dedicated page. It never opens a form.
    • Nothing is gated to be counted. Reading, browsing and comparing require no account. Accounts are created inside Post Property, Post Requirement and the SuperPro application, and nowhere else.
    • No fabricated proof. No invented statistics, no fake project names, no unverifiable claims. Early-stage numbers are stated as they are: non-round and small reads as true, "10,000+" reads as marketing.
    • A quote is never truncated. Shortening what a named person said misrepresents them. Length is an editorial cap enforced before publish, never an ellipsis at render.
    03

    Mobile-first, and breakpoints from content

    The most expensive lesson in this chapter

    Default CSS targets the phone. Desktop is layered on with min-width, never the reverse. That part is settled. The part that keeps going wrong is which number to put in the media query.

    Set the breakpoint from the width the component needsMeasured, not chosen from the device ladder

    Three separate iPad bugs, found in one audit, all had the same cause: a breakpoint picked from the device ladder (744, 600) instead of from the width the component measurably requires. For a row that requirement is sum(children) + gaps + container padding. Add it up before choosing the number.

    ComponentFired atActually needsSymptom
    Nav L2 merge7441080Grid column collapsed to 0; the logo drew through the tabs with 74px of overlap
    .br-finder / .pe-finder6001280 full, 1024 compactThe "OR" divider stranded alone on a wrapped line, across 680px of viewport range
    .vx-heronone (100svh)a ceiling387px of content floating in a 1114px field
    • A comment saying "desktop only" is not a breakpoint. The nav module's own comment read "DESKTOP ONLY, deliberately" directly above min-width:744px. Trust the number, and fix the prose when you fix the number.
    • Three bands beat a forced binary. When a component cannot fit a middle range, add a compact band rather than breaking it in half. The finder settled at <1024 modal, 1024-1279 compact one-line, ≥1280 full.
    • Make the pinned element fluid to win a compact band. width:min(720px,100%) held 720px even when the row could not afford it. flex:1 1 auto; max-width:720px plus flex-wrap:nowrap makes one line structural, leaving no wrap state for a divider to strand on.
    • Size a fixed input to its placeholder, measured with a hidden span at the input's own font, not to a round number. 200px clipped mid-word where the real requirement was 230.
    • Keep the JS and CSS breakpoints paired in a comment at both sites. The nav merge and the finder modal each had a media query and a matchMedia guard that had to move together. Undocumented, the next edit desynchronises them and one side styles a state the other never builds.
    • align-self never sets width on a grid item. align-self:flex-start on a CTA inside a display:grid card controls the block axis only; the 222px pill rendered at 654px. justify-self:start is the fix. A full-bleed pill reads as a banner, not a button.
    Length gets width, not smaller typeFor any editor-supplied text

    The /voices hero sized its quote with four tiers that all shrank the font, so the longer and more interesting the statement, the smaller it was set. Length was demoting the piece. The box was pinned at 620px inside a 900px measure, leaving 280px unused while the type shrank to fit.

    154-char quote at 1440Pinned 620pxWidth tiers
    Type size25px27px
    Lines43
    Box height188px159px
    • Check for unused width before reaching for a size cut. Bigger type, fewer lines and a shorter box, all from widening instead of shrinking. Shrink type only as a last-resort safety net, and say so in the comment.
    • On mobile the lever is alignment, not size. Width is already spent, so past roughly three lines switch centred to left. Centring reads as a slab at five lines. Use text-wrap:pretty for left-aligned copy and balance only for centred.
    • Raising a max-width means re-measuring every absolutely positioned sibling, at every breakpoint. Widening the quote bubble put 22 of the decorative glyph's 32px behind it. Measuring properly showed it already overlapped by 8px at 768 on every tier, a defect nobody had ever measured. Capping the box to protect the glyph cost a line of copy, so the decoration lost. Content beats ornament.
    • Measure before redesigning around the fold. The hero never exceeded its min-height at 1440 or 390x844. The only real overflow was 390x667 past 210 characters, by 10px.
    Section layout on mobileTwo rules, both from /voices
    • The section CTA sits below the cards, never between the title and the cards. Desktop is title left and button right on one row; below 744px the button moves under the content. Match on the head, not on a section class, so it cannot drift: .dp-strip, main > section:has(> .dp-strip__head){ display:flex; flex-direction:column; } then order:3 on the link. The trap is that order only applies to flex and grid items, so the section itself must become a flex column or the rule is silently inert.
    • Never leave a lone sideways-scrolling section. A page whose only mobile interaction is one horizontal rail reads as broken. Pair it with stacked content above or below.
    04

    Touch and gesture

    Where the phone behaves differently, not just smaller
    RuleValueWhy
    Minimum touch target44px in both axesAnything smaller is a mis-tap. Pad the hit area rather than growing the glyph
    Carousel gesturetouch-action: pan-y plus an 8px direction thresholdVertical page scroll must win until the reader has clearly committed to a horizontal drag
    Scroll chainingoverscroll-behavior: contain on every scrollable panelStops a modal's scroll leaking into the page behind it
    AutoplayIntersectionObserver, threshold: 0.15A carousel that animates off-screen burns battery and data for nothing
    ⚠
    Trap Touch hover sticks. A tapped element stays in :hover until something else is tapped, so any global @media (hover: none){ *:hover{ transform:none !important } } rule will silently freeze every transform-positioned element, including off-canvas panels and modals. Exclude layout elements at the source of that rule, never with !important on each animating element. Documented in full at Chapter 09.
    44px, drawnThe dashed line is the hit area, not the glyph

    The icon is 16px in both rows. Only the target around it changes. Pad the hit area rather than growing the glyph: a bigger icon changes the design, a bigger target only changes whether a thumb lands on it.

    28px · mis-taps

    44px · the floor

    05

    Scroll, overlays and the nav

    The rules that keep chrome from disappearing
    Blocking scroll behind an overlayNever with position:fixed on body
    • GSAP ScrollSmoother is active on desktop at ≥744px. Setting position:fixed on <body> to lock scroll fights it and loses the reader's place. Block with wheel and touchmove prevention instead.
    • Allow scrolling inside the panel itself with an event.target.closest() check against the open surface.
    • Each off-canvas L1 and L2 panel is its own scroll container, so one panel's position never bleeds into another's.
    • The menu resets to the top on every open. A reader who reopens a menu is starting a new intent, not resuming the last one.
    The nav collapse gateHiding the masthead is a handoff, never a way to reclaim 80px

    The masthead may translate away only when a separate second-level bar is there to take the top of the viewport. The single predicate is window.gharCanCollapseNav() in main.js, which tests whether --subnav-h is greater than zero. That variable is published from a measured height by each page's syncH(), so no page needs to know the breakpoint or inspect markup.

    Situation--subnav-hMay hide L1
    Mobile, page has an L2 bar~65Yes, L2 takes the top
    Desktop, L2 merged into L10No
    Page has no L2 at all0No
    • Any page that toggles mainnav-hidden must AND it with the gate: classList.toggle('mainnav-hidden', shouldCollapse && !!(window.gharCanCollapseNav && window.gharCanCollapseNav())).
    • Above 744px the merge module moves .subnav-inner into #navTabs inside the masthead. Hiding L1 there takes the section nav with it and leaves the page with no chrome at all.
    • Pages whose handoff target is a sticky in-page finder rather than an L2 bar (/brands, /people, person profiles, voices-search) do not use this gate. They gate on their own threshold against the search wrap, and that behaviour is settled. Do not "fix" them with this.
    Inner-page navbody.simple-nav
    • One 760px search pill, 56px tall, centred in an 80px nav bar, at every viewport. No shrink, no shadow toggle, no scroll-induced change: main.js early-returns for body.simple-nav.
    • Below 744px the same content renders in #mobSearchTrigger, padding overridden to hold the identical 56px height.
    • The search modal is full-screen white below 744px and a centred card above it. Clicking the backdrop closes; clicking the card does not.
    • The property filter button is deliberately deleted on these pages. It belongs to property search and property detail only.
    06

    Loading and empty

    Four counts, every section

    Ghar.tv is backend-driven. Item counts are never fixed, so "it looks fine because we have three cards today" is not a finished section. Every section must survive N=0, N=1, N=expected and N far beyond expected before it ships.

    CountWhat must happen
    N = 0The section collapses entirely, or shows a meaningful empty state with a next action. Never a header and a "See all" link above nothing.
    N = 1The single item sits at its natural width. It never stretches across a slot sized for three, and it leaves no gap that reads as missing content.
    N = expectedThe happy path, as designed.
    N >> expectedAbsorbed by a carousel, a wrap or paging. Never a broken horizontal row.
    • Skeletons, not spinners, for cards and rails. A skeleton keeps the layout stable so nothing jumps when data lands. A spinner over an empty region tells the reader nothing about what is coming.
    • Never spin on empty. If the result set is genuinely empty, say so and offer the next move. An indefinite spinner is the interface refusing to answer.
    • Buttons carry their own pending state inline, and stay disabled only while the request is in flight.
    • Images that arrive from the backend go inside an aspect-* wrapper. Locking the ratio on the container instead of the image is what keeps a grid aligned when the source dimensions vary.
    • The full defensive class table, and the list of sections that still assume a fixed count, is in Chapter 10.
    All four countsThe same section, four backend responses

    One section, one set of rules, switched through every count the backend can actually return. Watch what the "See all" link does at zero, and what the single card does at one.

    Items returned
    Recently added See all →

    07

    Errors and recovery

    Say what happened and what to do
    FailureSurfaceRule
    One field is wrongInline, below the fieldNamed field, plain cause, and the shape of a valid answer. Shown after the reader leaves the field, not while typing.
    The submit failedToast, plus the form left intactNever clear what was typed. Offer retry.
    A section could not loadThe section's own empty stateThe rest of the page stays usable. One failed rail does not take the page down.
    The page does not existFull page, in brandSearch and the main verticals as the next move, never a bare 404.
    • No raw codes, no stack text, no internal names. "Something went wrong (500)" is not a message. Name the action that failed.
    • Errors do not apologise and are never vague. They state what happened and how to fix it, in the interface's voice.
    • An empty screen is an invitation to act, not a mood. Every empty state carries one clear next step.
    • Announce errors to assistive tech with role="alert" or an aria-live="polite" region. A message that only exists visually does not exist for everyone.
    08

    Interface writing

    Words are design material
    • Name things by what the reader controls, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config.
    • An action keeps its name through the whole flow. The button that says Publish produces a toast that says Published. The vocabulary is the signposting.
    • Active voice, sentence case, plain verbs. "Save changes", not "Submit". Specific always beats clever.
    • One element, one job. A label labels, an example demonstrates. Nothing quietly does double duty.
    • Indian conventions throughout. Rupees as ₹, never a dollar sign. Lakhs and crores, not millions. Dates as DD/MM. Square feet, and carpet or built-up stated explicitly rather than assumed.
    • Never an em dash. Restructure the sentence, or use a comma, a colon or a full stop.
    • Reference brands and raw platform URLs are internal vocabulary. Neither appears in user-facing copy.
    09

    Accessibility

    The floor, checked on every component
    AreaRequirementWhere it usually breaks here
    FocusVisible :focus-visible on everything interactiveRemoved because the ring "looked wrong" on a card. Restyle it, never delete it.
    ContrastAA against the surface the text actually sits on--faint on a sand or turmeric panel, not on white
    Touch target44px minimumIcon-only buttons in dense rows, and paginator dots
    Motionprefers-reduced-motion snaps to the end stateNew reveals that ship before the fallback block
    ImagesReal alt, or alt="" when decorativeBrand logos in tiles, portraits in card grids
    KeyboardEvery drag or hover affordance has a keyboard pathCarousels: arrows must be reachable and the track focusable
    SemanticsHeadings in order, landmarks present, state announcedAccordions and tabs built from divs without aria-expanded
    • A hover-only affordance is a broken affordance. Anything revealed on hover needs a focus path and a touch path. Carousel arrows that appear only on hover fail on every phone.
    • Colour is never the only signal. A state that reads only as red is invisible to a large share of readers. Pair it with an icon, a label or a shape.
    • Test with the keyboard before calling a component done. Tab through it, operate it, and confirm focus never disappears into a hidden panel.

    Social & Video

    00

    The five rules that never bend

    Break one and the post gets pulled, not corrected
    • Red is the logo and one action, nothing else. #ee324b covers the mark and a single call to action per frame. It is never an eyebrow, a hashtag, a date, a bullet or a border. Roughly five percent of any frame, maximum.
    • The wordmark never sits beside a shape glyph. One or the other in a frame, never both. The logo is also never typed: always the supplied SVG, never Gazpacho or Inter set to "Ghar.tv".
    • Gazpacho is display only. Headlines and pull quotes. Every label, caption, handle, subtitle and body line is Inter. Gazpacho is never italicised and never takes negative tracking.
    • Nothing lands in a platform safe band. Copy and logo stay inside the live area marked in Stories, reels and video. A caption under a progress bar is a caption nobody reads.
    • No invented numbers. Stats come from a published Intelligence report and carry its name. If a figure has no source, the frame ships without it.

    03

    Colour

    Not which colours exist, but which one this post has earned

    The seventeen values and their hex codes live in Chapter 01, which is the only place they are listed. Re-printing them here would guarantee that one copy eventually drifts from the other. This section answers the question Chapter 01 does not: standing in front of a blank 1080 canvas, which colour do you reach for, how much of it, and when is the honest answer none.

    Open the full palette in Chapter 01
    The earning testFour questions, before any colour goes on a canvas

    A colour is not a decoration budget you are obliged to spend. It has to be doing a job that the type, the photograph and the layout are not already doing. If a colour fails any one of these, the frame is finished without it.

    • 1. Is it carrying meaning? Name the meaning out loud. "Turmeric because this is a GharTalks episode" is a reason. "Turmeric because the post looked plain" is not, and produces a feed where colour means nothing because it means everything.
    • 2. Would the frame be worse without it? Delete the colour and look again. Warm white with ink type and one good photograph is the house default, not a fallback. Most posts are finished at that point.
    • 3. Is it the only accent here? One theme colour per frame. A second is not twice as expressive, it is a frame with no point of view.
    • 4. Does it survive the platform? The feed compresses, crops and sits it beside a competitor's post. A tone that only works at full size, or only against the canvas you designed on, has not earned the frame.
    How muchCoverage of a single 1080 frame
    TierShare of the frameWhat it may paintWhat it may never paint
    Foundation
    white, warm white, rule, ink, espresso, muted    		85 to 100%The ground, all body type, dividers, captions, the safe areasNothing is off limits. This is the canvas
    One theme colour
    turmeric, terracotta, sage, indigo, aubergine    		0 to 15%One panel, one rule, one filled shape, one word set apart, a category tagTwo of them in one frame. A gradient between them. Body copy
    Brand red #ee324bUnder 5%, and often zeroThe logo, and a single primary actionEyebrows, dates, category tags, quote marks, decorative dots, borders, bullets, hover states on ordinary text
    Brand tints
    rose, blush, petal, mist    		A quiet ground, or a chip fillSoft panels behind a quote, chip and tag fills, a story backgroundType at any size. They are grounds, not inks

    The 15% figure is a ceiling, not a target. A run of ten posts where every frame spends its full 15% reads as a brand shouting continuously. Colour is legible as emphasis only when most frames do without it.

    Which oneColour by meaning, never by rotation for variety
    SubjectReach forBecause
    GharTalks, conversation, a person speakingTurmeric #eda41cWarm, awake, human. It is the closest tone to a lit room
    Architecture, materials, craft, makingTerracotta #d5613aIt is a material colour before it is a brand colour: brick, clay, earth
    Green building, infrastructure, long-term valueSage #9aa96dGrowth without the cliche of a bright green
    Intelligence, data, rankings, market analysisIndigo #5f71a9Cool and measured. The one tone that reads as evidence rather than opinion
    Design, interiors, luxury, the aspirational endAubergine #895772The richest tone in the set. Rare, so it stays an event
    Property, listings, an ordinary editorial postNone. Warm white and a photographMost posts. The photograph is already carrying the colour
    A Ghar.tv announcement or a primary actionBrand red, on the mark or one buttonThe only place red is not decoration
    • The same subject keeps the same colour across the whole run. A GharTalks post that is turmeric this week and indigo next week has taught the reader nothing. Consistency is the entire value of a coded palette.
    • Do not rotate for variety. If three posts in a row are all architecture, all three are terracotta. A feed that alternates tone to look interesting is a feed where tone carries no information.
    • Blend theme with theme only. A theme colour mixed into a foundation tone goes muddy every time. Keep them separate, or use the pure value.
    • No two-stop gradient as a background. Flat solid, or a committed dark panel. If depth is wanted, get it from typographic contrast or a photograph.
    Pairings, checked liveRatios computed in your browser, not typed in by hand

    Every pairing below is measured against WCAG when the page loads, from the same two hex values the chip is painted with. 4.5:1 is the floor for body copy, 3:1 for display type at 24px bold and above. Read the two flags separately: a pairing that fails BODY but passes DISPLAY is usable for a headline or a button label and must never carry a paragraph.

    White on turmeric and white on sage are house pairings. They are a brand decision, not a threshold result, which is why they carry that label instead of a score. The measured ratio is still shown because it tells you what the pairing needs to work: set it at display weight, Gazpacho or Inter 600 and up, at 24px or larger on a 1080 canvas. Do not run small body copy or a caption in white on either. For a paragraph on those grounds, use ink, which measures 8.44:1 and 7.03:1. Second, brand red is not a body-copy background. White on #ee324b measures 4.04:1, which clears the display floor and misses the body floor. It is correct for the logo and for a button label set at 600 weight; it is wrong for a sentence. This is also why a filled CTA on a tenant page uses ink rather than the tenant hex: ink on white is 15.9:1 for every tenant, and an arbitrary brand colour cannot be guaranteed to clear either floor.

    The same post, three colour budgetsIdentical content and layout

    One post, three amounts of colour. The middle one is the house default and the one most posts should look like. The right-hand one is what happens when colour is treated as a decoration budget that has to be spent.

    Logo

    The rules with no exceptions
    Clear spaceProportional, so it holds at any size
    G
    Keep clear space equal to the height of the G on all four sides. Nothing enters it: no text, no shape, no photograph edge, no other logo.
    • Never typed. The wordmark is always the supplied SVG or PNG. Setting "Ghar.tv" in Gazpacho or Inter does not make a logo.
    • Never beside a shape glyph. One or the other in a frame.
    • Never recoloured beyond the approved on-light and on-dark versions. No gradients, no outlines, no shadows, no rotation.
    • Minimum size is 24px tall on screen. Below that, use the G mark alone.
    • On a photograph, place it only where contrast is genuinely sufficient. If it needs a scrim to be legible, move it.

    06

    Shapes and photography

    What goes in a frame besides type

    Nine canonical silhouettes, each a roof and house-body variant of the logo G. They are design moves, not category icons: a shape does not stand for a topic, and the same shape can appear across different pillars.

    • One shape per frame. Two competing silhouettes read as clip art.
    • A shape may hold a photograph as a mask at display scale. Never at small inline size, where the mask reads as a smudge.
    • Shapes may sit on photography in social, print, merchandise and editorial. Not in product UI.
    • Grab them from 9 Canonical Shapes: Copy for markup, SVG for a file, PNG for a transparent 1024 square in the shape's colour.
    Photography directionOwned by Imagery & Shapes
    • Warm, natural light. Real interiors and real architecture. Nothing that looks like generic stock.
    • Indian or relatable Asian faces whenever a human subject appears. This is an Indian platform and the audience notices immediately when it is not.
    • When a confirmed Indian face is not available, use no face at all. Property aerials, city skylines, material close-ups. These read universally and are always safer than a wrong face.
    • Photographs lead without overlays wherever possible. The image is the story, not a backdrop for type.
    • A named individual is shown with their real photograph or not at all. Never a stand-in portrait for a real person.
    UseAspect
    Property photography4:3
    Hero and landscape video16:9
    Discovery grids, square posts1:1
    Editorial and portrait posts4:5
    Stories, reels, shorts9:16

    • Every social cut ships sound off by default. If the piece does not work muted with subtitles, it is not finished.

    Shooting and framingDecisions that cannot be fixed in the edit
    • Shoot for the vertical crop from the start. Frame the 16:9 so the subject sits inside the middle 9:16 of it. Reframing afterwards is what puts heads in the top safe band.
    • Interviews: subject slightly off centre, looking across the empty side of the frame, eyeline near the upper third. Headroom tight, never a hand's width of ceiling.
    • Backgrounds are real rooms. A project, a studio, a site. Never a seamless backdrop and never a blurred hotel lobby.
    • Natural light where possible, matching the photography direction: warm, soft, directional. If you light it, light it to look like a window.
    • Record room tone for thirty seconds at every location. It is free, and it is the only thing that fixes an audio edit later.
    • Shoot b-roll of the space, the materials and the hands. Talking-head-only edits have nothing to cut away to and always feel longer than they are.

    TransitionsStraight cut. Cross dissolve only between locationsWipes, spins, zooms and glitch effects read as amateur and date instantly
    OpeningStart on the most interesting frame, no logo sting firstThe first second decides whether the rest is watched
    Shot length2 to 5 seconds in a reel, longer in an interviewCut on motion or on a completed thought, never on a fixed beat count
    Text on screenHolds long enough to read twiceA viewer is also reading a caption and watching the picture
    MusicLicensed, credited in the project file, under the dialogue at roughly -18 LUFSAn unlicensed track gets the post muted or pulled
    DialogueAround -16 LUFS, ducked music beneath itSpeech is the content; music is furniture
    ColourRec.709, gentle grade toward the warm paletteA heavy LUT pulls the picture away from the brand tones
    LogoStatic, on the end card onlyAn animated logo on every cut is a tell, not a brand
    YouTube thumbnailA separate deliverable, not a frame grab
    PropertyValue
    Canvas1280 × 720, under 2 MB
    TextFour words maximum, Gazpacho, large enough to read at 210px wide
    FaceOne face, looking at camera, occupying roughly a third of the frame
    Safe cornerKeep the bottom right clear; the duration badge sits there
    NeverRed arrows, circles, shocked expressions, fake play buttons
    Deliverables per shootWhat comes back from every commission
    • The graded master at 1920 × 1080, kept in full quality. Platforms re-encode, and re-exporting from a delivery file compounds the damage.
    • A vertical cut at 1080 × 1920 with burned-in subtitles.
    • One teaser, 30 to 60 seconds, in both aspects.
    • A thumbnail at 1280 × 720.
    • Three to five stills pulled from the shoot, full resolution, for the social team to use as posts.
    • A subtitle file (.srt) alongside the burned-in version, for the site player and for accessibility.
    • The music licence reference, in writing.
    11

    Quote cards

    The format we publish most, and misuse most

    A quote card is the words and the person who said them. The temptation is to decorate it. Resist: the quote carries the frame, the attribution grounds it, and everything else is subtraction.

    Anatomy4:5 default
    Industry Voices
    A home is the only thing most people buy without ever seeing it built.
    Hafeez Contractor · Architect
    Text only
    the default
    Industry Voices
    A home is the only thing most people buy without ever seeing it built.
    Hafeez Contractor · Architect
    With a field mark
    one shape, never beside the logo
    • Quote sets in Gazpacho 700 at 76–104px. If it does not fit in three lines at 76px, the pull quote is too long. Trim the quote.
    • Curly quotation marks belong in the copy. No giant decorative quote glyph, and if one is used it is --ink at 10% opacity, never red.
    • Attribution is name, then role, separated by a middot. No company logo on the card.
    • A photo-masked shape is allowed at display scale only. Never at inline size, where the mask reads as a smudge.
    • Quote copy is verbatim. Tighten with an ellipsis if you must, never paraphrase into quotation marks.
    12

    Announcements

    Five things we announce, one shape each

    An announcement earns the one red call to action per frame. Everything else stays quiet so the action is unmissable. Each type below has a fixed structure, so the reader learns to recognise it.

    TypesStructure is fixed, copy is not
    TypeEyebrowCarriesAction
    Property launchNow listedConfiguration, locality, price in lakhs or croresSee the listing
    GharTalks episodeNew episodeGuest name, role, episode numberListen now
    GharEvents dateSave the dateEvent name, city, date as DD/MMRegister
    Architecture & Design featureNew featureProject, architect, cityRead the story
    Industry Voices interviewNew interviewName, role, the sharpest lineRead the interview
    • Dates are DD/MM. Money is lakhs and crores with the rupee sign, never a dollar figure and never "4.2M".
    • One action per frame. Two calls to action means the reader takes neither.
    • An event with no confirmed date says "dates soon", never a placeholder date.
    13

    Voice and hashtags

    How the caption sounds

    We sound like someone who knows the market explaining it to a friend who is about to spend a lot of money. Intelligent, plain, never breathless. The caption adds what the frame does not already say; it never repeats the headline back.

    Write this
    Registrations held flat through August, against a monsoon that usually takes ten percent off. The full read is in this month's report. Says something the frame did not. Gives a reason to tap.
    Not this
    🔥 HUGE news! Mumbai registrations are holding STRONG 💪 You won't believe what happens next. Link in bio!! 🏠✨ Emoji as punctuation, a promise the story does not keep, and nothing learned.
    Caption patternThree moves, in order
    • Open with the fact. The most specific true thing, in one sentence. No question openers, no "Did you know".
    • Add the context the frame could not hold. One or two sentences. This is the part worth reading.
    • Point somewhere. One destination, named plainly. "The full report" beats "Link in bio".
    RuleDetail
    LengthUnder 60 words. The first 12 are what most people read
    EmojiNone in the first line. At most one elsewhere, and only if it carries meaning
    CaseSentence case. Never all caps for emphasis
    NumbersLakhs and crores. Sq ft, not sqft. DD/MM dates
    NamesFull name on first mention, role after a middot
    HashtagsThree to five, never a wall

    One pillar tag, one or two topic tags, one city tag when the post is local. Tags are written in camel case so they stay readable.

    #GharTv #GharTalks #GharEvents #GharIntelligence #IndianArchitecture #IndianHomes #RealEstateIndia #MumbaiRealEstate #BengaluruRealEstate
    • #GharTv goes on everything. It is the only tag that is not optional.
    • No engagement bait tags. No #followforfollow, no #viral, no tag unrelated to the post.
    • Tags sit at the end of the caption, never scattered through the sentences.
    14

    Accessibility and disclosure

    The parts that are not taste

    Everything above is craft and can be argued. This section is not. A frame that fails here does not go out, however good it looks.

    LegibilityChecked before export, not after posting
    • Contrast 4.5:1 minimum for any text meant to be read, measured against what is actually behind it. Over a photograph, measure against the lightest patch the type crosses, not the average.
    • Captions on every video. Social plays muted by default, so a video without burned-in subtitles reaches a fraction of its audience and excludes deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers entirely. This is not optional.
    • Alt text on every image post. Describe what is in the frame and what it means, in one sentence. "Courtyard of a Bengaluru home, open to the sky, with a stone floor" beats "image" and beats a list of hashtags.
    • Never colour alone to carry meaning. Pair it with a label, a shape or a position.
    • No flashing faster than three times a second, in any cut. It is a seizure risk.
    • Type below 28px on a 1080 canvas is decoration, not information. Assume nobody reads it.
    Paid and partnered contentLabel it, always

    Anything a brand paid for or supplied carries a label, on the frame itself and in the caption. The platform's own paid-partnership tool is used as well, not instead.

    RelationshipLabelUse when
    Brand funded the piece, we made itIn Collaboration WithEditorial control stayed with us
    Brand owns the piecePresented ByThe brand shaped the content
    Product or stay was giftedGiftedNothing was paid but something was received
    • The label is never smaller than the eyebrow and never sits in a safe band where the platform will cover it.
    • Sponsorship attaches to a card or a piece, never to a section header, a topic strip or the account itself.
    • Photographs carry their credit. A photographer's name is not optional because the frame is small.
    • Quote a person only from something they actually said on record. Verbatim, trimmed with an ellipsis at most.
    15

    The brief, for an AI tool

    Paste this before you ask for anything

    Everything above, compressed into constraints a model can follow. Paste it as a system prompt or at the top of a chat, then make your request. It is deliberately blunt: a flat list of rules produces on-brand output far more reliably than a description of the design philosophy. Re-copy it whenever this chapter changes, since it is maintained by hand.

    Ghar.tv brand brief
    You are producing social media and video content for Ghar.tv. Follow these rules exactly.

BRAND
Ghar.tv is India's real estate discovery, intelligence, media and events platform. It is not a listing portal. Tagline: "Real Estate. For You."
Positioning: understanding-first, not transaction-first. We help people understand the market before they transact.
Personality: intelligent, empowering, trustworthy, editorial, premium, calm.

VOICE
Write like someone who knows the market explaining it to a friend who is about to spend a lot of money.
Plain verbs. Sentence case. Specific over clever. Active voice.
Never: hype, breathlessness, emoji as punctuation, ALL CAPS for emphasis, clickbait, "Did you know", "You won't believe", "Link in bio" as the only direction.
Never use em dashes. Use commas, colons or full stops.
Say "Industry Voices", never "arguments", "takes", "claims" or "hot takes".
Product names stand alone: GharTalks, GharEvents, VideoWorks, Brand Connect, SuperPro, Intelligence.

CAPTIONS
Three moves in order: (1) open with the most specific true fact in one sentence, (2) add the context the image could not hold, (3) point to one destination, named plainly.
Under 60 words. The first 12 carry it. No emoji in the first line, at most one elsewhere and only if it means something.
Hashtags at the end, three to five, camel case. #GharTv on everything. One pillar tag, one or two topic tags, one city tag if local.
Never engagement bait: no #viral, no #followforfollow, no unrelated tags.

NUMBERS AND FORMATS
Indian conventions only. Rupees, and lakhs and crores, never dollars and never "4.2M". Write ₹4.2 Cr.
Dates as DD/MM. Areas as "sq ft".
Never invent a statistic. Every figure names the published report it came from, or it is cut.
Never invent project names, client names, or awards.

COLOUR (hex is exact)
Foundation: White #ffffff, Warm White #faf7f2, Rule #e5dcc8, Sand #e0c199, Muted #6e655b, Espresso #3a2f27, Ink #1a1714.
Brand: Brand Red #ee324b, Rose #f37e86, Blush #f6aaad, Petal #fbd4d5, Mist #fde8e8.
Theme: Turmeric #eda41c, Terracotta #d5613a, Sage #9aa96d, Indigo #5f71a9, Aubergine #895772.
Brand Red is ONLY the logo and one call to action per frame. Roughly 5% of a frame maximum. It is never an eyebrow, hashtag, date, bullet, border, quote mark or decorative dot.
One theme colour per frame, chosen because it matches the subject, not for variety. Do not blend a theme colour with a foundation tone. No two-stop gradient backgrounds.
Text contrast 4.5:1 minimum.

TYPE
Gazpacho Bold: headlines, pull quotes and any number over 14px. Line height 1.08. Default tracking.
Inter: everything else, weights 400 to 700. Body line height 1.6 to 1.8.
Suiza SemiBold: the logo tagline only. Never a heading or body font.
Never set a headline in Inter. Never set body copy in Gazpacho. Never italicise Gazpacho.

LOGO
Always the supplied SVG or PNG file, never typed out in a font.
Clear space equal to the height of the G on all sides. Minimum 24px tall; below that use the G mark alone.
Never beside a shape glyph. Never recoloured, outlined, shadowed or rotated.

SHAPES
Nine canonical house silhouettes, each a variant of the logo G. One per frame. They are design moves, not category icons.
A shape may mask a photograph at display scale only.

IMAGERY
Warm natural light, real interiors and real architecture, nothing generic-stock.
Indian or relatable Asian faces whenever a person appears. If a confirmed Indian face is unavailable, use no face: aerials, skylines, material close-ups.
A named individual appears with their real photograph or not at all.

CANVAS SIZES
Square post 1080x1080. Portrait post 1080x1350 (default for Instagram and Facebook). Story and Reel 1080x1920. Landscape video 1920x1080. Avatar 800x800.
Margin 72px on a 1080 canvas.
On a 1080x1920 vertical frame, keep everything inside the live area: top band 250px and bottom band 320px belong to the platform's interface, side margins 64px. Live area is 952x1350.

VIDEO
Every social cut must work with sound off. Burned-in subtitles, Inter 700 at 48px, white with a soft shadow, never a solid box, two lines maximum, above the bottom safe band.
Lower third: name in Inter 700 at 44px, role beneath in Inter 500 at 30px, white plate at 95% with a 3px Brand Red left rule. This is the one red element in an edit.
Reels and Shorts 15 to 45 seconds. Export H.264, AAC 192kbps 48kHz, audio peaks at -1 dBTP, Rec.709 colour, match the source frame rate.
End card holds 2 seconds: one line, the handle, nothing animated.

CONTENT PILLARS
GharTalks (conversations), Intelligence (data and reports), Architecture & Design (spaces and the people behind them), Industry Voices (written perspectives), GharEvents (the four signature shows), Properties (listings and launches).
Every piece belongs to exactly one pillar, which sets the eyebrow and the tag.

DISCLOSURE
Paid or partnered work is always labelled on the frame and in the caption: "In Collaboration With" when we kept editorial control, "Presented By" when the brand shaped it, "Gifted" when something was received.
Sponsorship attaches to a single piece, never to a section or the account.

ALWAYS
Alt text on every image. Captions on every video. Credit every photographer.

NEVER
Never name a competitor platform or a reference brand in public copy.
Never promise a return, a price movement or an investment outcome.
Never use a stock photo of a person to stand in for a real named individual.
    ⚠
    An AI does not check facts This brief constrains style and format, and it tells a model not to invent figures, but a model will still produce a confident wrong number if pushed. Every statistic, name, date and price in generated copy gets checked against the source before it goes out. The brief makes output on brand; it does not make it true.
    07

    Print & Brand.

    For graphic designers

    What changes off screen, colour converted to CMYK with its honest limits, the logo in millimetres, typography in points, the page grid with bleed and safety, stationery and collateral at true proportion, and large format sized by viewing distance. Ends with a pre-flight checklist to run before any file leaves.

    01

    What changes off screen

    The four things print does not forgive

    The brand is the same brand on paper. What changes is that nothing can be corrected after the fact: a screen re-renders, a print run does not. These four are where digital habits cost money.

    The fourIn the order they usually go wrong
    On screenOn paperWhat to do
    RGB, backlit, effectively unlimited gamutCMYK, reflected, a much smaller gamut. Vivid colours go flatCheck every brand colour against the CMYK table below before approving a proof. Brand red is the one that shifts most
    A pixel is a pixelInk spreads into the fibre (dot gain), so small type fills in and fine reverses close upNothing under 6pt. No hairlines under 0.25pt. No reversed type under 8pt
    The canvas edge is the edgeThe guillotine moves. There is no edge, only a tolerance3mm bleed, 3mm trim, and keep everything that matters inside the safety margin
    Fonts load or they do notFonts must be embedded or outlined, or the RIP substitutes silentlyOutline display type, embed the rest, and always check the PDF's font list before release
    02

    Colour in CMYK

    Converted live, with the honest caveats

    Every value below is converted in your browser from the same hex the swatch is painted with, so the table cannot drift from Chapter 01. These are unmanaged conversions: a naive RGB to CMYK transform with no ICC profile and no press condition. They are the right starting point and the wrong finishing point. Convert through the printer's own profile and sign a proof.

    Brand red is out of gamutThe one that will disappoint you
    • A vivid red at this saturation cannot be reproduced in four-colour process. It converts to roughly M79 Y68 and prints noticeably duller and flatter than the screen. Everyone is surprised by this once.
    • If the red matters, print it as a spot colour. That is what a fifth plate is for, and on a cover, a card or an identity piece it is worth the money. On a two-page internal handout it is not.
    • Never colour-match a spot to a screen. A Pantone number has to be chosen against a physical guide, under standardised light, on the actual stock. No number is printed in this document, because a fabricated one would be trusted and would be wrong. Ask the printer to pull the nearest chip to #ee324b on coated and on uncoated, and record both here once they are confirmed.
    • Uncoated stock absorbs more ink and reads darker and duller than coated. A colour approved on coated is not approved on uncoated.
    BlacksFlat black is a mistake at any size above a caption
    UseBuildWhy
    Body text, rules, small typeK100 onlyA single plate cannot misregister against itself. Multi-plate text shows colour fringes on any shift
    Large ink areas, covers, panelsRich black C60 M40 Y40 K100K100 alone over a large area looks washed and grey. The under-colour gives it depth
    The brand's Ink where it must match the digital toneC0 M12 Y23 K90, warmed#1a1714 is a warm near-black, not a neutral. A neutral black next to it reads blue
    NeverRich black under small textRegistration is never perfect and 8pt type in four plates is unreadable
    • Total ink coverage stays under 300% on coated and under 260% on uncoated or newsprint. The swatches above flag anything heavy. Exceed it and the sheet cannot dry, which shows as set-off on the back of the next sheet.
    • Overprint the black text, knock out everything else, unless the printer says otherwise for that job.
    StockThe paper is part of the palette
    PieceStockNote
    Business card300 to 350gsm uncoatedUncoated suits the warm palette. Gloss lamination fights it
    Letterhead100 to 120gsm uncoatedMust take a desktop printer and a pen
    Brochure cover250 to 300gsm, matt laminatedMatt, never gloss. Gloss reads as a flyer
    Brochure inner130 to 170gsm silkSilk holds photography without the glare of gloss
    Event poster170gsm silk

    The warm white in the palette is a screen value. On paper, do not print it: choose a stock whose own white is close to it and leave the sheet unprinted. Printing a near-white flood over an already-white sheet costs ink, risks banding, and always looks slightly dirty next to the true paper at the trim edge.

    03

    The logo in print

    Minimum sizes in millimetres

    Same discipline as on screen, expressed in physical units. The vector files are in Chapter 01: use the SVG, never a PNG, and never a screenshot.

    Minimum sizesBelow these the counters fill in
    AssetMinimum widthClear zone
    Full wordmark22mm litho, 28mm screen print or uncoatedThe height of the G on every side
    G mark7mm litho, 10mm screen print, 12mm embroideredHalf the mark's height on every side
    Foil, emboss or deboss30mm wordmarkSame, plus 5mm from any trim edge
    • The clear zone is proportional, so it holds at any size. Nothing enters it: no type, no rule, no image edge, no fold, no trim.
    • Three colourways only, exactly as on screen: brand red, white, or ink. On a photograph, white. Never a tint of the red, never a gradient, never an outline, never a drop shadow.
    • Never paired with a canonical shape. The nine shapes are a supporting vocabulary; putting one beside the mark creates a second logo.
    • Never redrawn or re-spaced. If it does not fit, the layout is wrong, not the mark.
    • For a single-colour job, the mark is ink or white. A red mark on a one-colour black job is not an option, it is a second plate.
    04

    Typography in points

    Two faces, and the one that is missing
    HierarchyA4 and smaller. Scale up for large format
    RoleFaceSize / leadingTracking
    Cover headlineGazpacho Bold48 to 72pt / 1.05Default. Never negative
    Section headGazpacho Bold24 to 32pt / 1.1Default
    StandfirstInter Regular13 to 15pt / 1.5Default
    BodyInter Regular9.5 to 10.5pt / 1.45Default
    Caption, creditInter Medium7.5 to 8pt / 1.4+0.01em
    Eyebrow, labelInter Semibold, caps7.5pt+0.1em
    Legal, disclaimerInter Regular6 to 6.5pt / 1.35Default. Never smaller than 6pt
    • Gazpacho keeps its default tracking at every size. Negative tracking closes the counters, and on paper they fill with ink as well.
    • No Gazpacho italic. There is no true italic and a mechanically slanted face is obvious at print resolution. Use weight or colour for emphasis.
    • Measure runs 60 to 72 characters. On A4 that is roughly a 105mm column, which is why the grid below is built in twelve columns rather than a single measure.
    • Hyphenation on for justified text, off for ragged. Never more than two consecutive hyphens, and never a hyphen across a column or page break.
    • Big numbers, prices and statistics are Gazpacho, matching the screen rule. Rupees as ₹, lakhs and crores, dates as DD/MM.
    ⚠
    Missing asset Suiza is specified for the tagline lockup, and brand_assets/SuizaDEMO-SemiBold.otf is not in the repository, so the tagline cannot be set outside a design tool and this page cannot render it. Until the licensed file is added, set the tagline in Inter Semibold and treat every Suiza reference in this chapter as pending.
    05

    The page

    Grid, margins, and the three edges
    Bleed, trim, safetyDrawn to scale
    Bleed +3mm
    Trim
    Safety
    Everything that must survive the cut lives in here
    EdgeValueRule
    Bleed3mm on every sideAny element touching the edge must extend into it. A background that stops at the trim will show a white sliver
    Safety5mm inside the trimNo type, logo or essential detail outside this. The guillotine tolerance is real
    Margin15mm A4, 5mm business cardThe design margin, not the tolerance. Usually larger than safety
    Gutter, bound workAdd 5mm to the inner marginPerfect binding swallows the inner edge. Never cross the gutter with a face or a word
    The gridTwelve columns, same reasoning as the screen
    • Twelve columns with a 5mm gutter on A4. Twelve divides into 2, 3, 4 and 6, so one grid carries a full-bleed image, a two-column feature, a three-column index and a caption rail without a second system.
    • A baseline grid of 12pt, with body at 10.5/1.45 sitting on every second line. Cross-column text that does not share a baseline is the clearest sign of an amateur layout.
    • One idea per spread. The same restraint as a screen section: a spread that carries a headline, a photograph and one caption is finished.
    • Photography follows the screen direction: warm, soft, directional light, real rooms and real people. Indian or relatable Asian faces where people appear. Minimum 300dpi at final size, and check that before laying it out, not after.
    • The canonical shapes may hold a photograph as a mask at spread scale, exactly as on screen. One shape per spread, never a row of them.
    06

    Stationery and collateral

    Shown at true proportion
    Business card and letterhead89 × 54mm and A4, to scale
    Name Surname
    Role · Ghar.tv
    +91 00000 00000
    name@ghar.tv · ghar.tv
    Card, face · 89 × 54mm
    Card, reverse · rich black
    Ghar.tv · ghar.tv · hello@ghar.tv
    Letterhead · A4
    • The card face carries the mark, the person and the contact. Nothing else. No QR code, no tagline, no address block, no social handles. The reverse is a rich-black field with the G mark centred, and that is the whole design.
    • The letterhead's mark sits top left at 20mm wide, with a 15mm margin all round and the legal line at the foot in 6pt. The body area must stay clear: someone has to be able to type a letter into it.
    • Envelope: mark top left only, at the same 20mm. Nothing on the reverse.
    • Brochures follow the twelve-column grid. Cover is one image, one headline and the mark. A cover with three messages has none.
    07

    Large format

    Hoardings, booths, signage

    Large format inverts the usual rules. Resolution goes down, not up, because the viewer is further away, and the only measurement that matters is the distance they read it from.

    Size by distanceThe one calculation to remember
    Read fromCap height, minimumArtwork resolution at final sizeTypical piece
    1m7mm150dpiBooth panel, table card
    3m20mm120dpiRoll-up banner, badge wall
    10m70mm72dpiBooth back-wall, stage
    30m200mm25dpiHoarding
    50m+350mm15dpiBuilding wrap

    The rule of thumb is 7mm of cap height per metre of viewing distance, and a little more for anything read while moving. Supplying a hoarding at 300dpi is not caution, it is a file nobody can open.

    Composition at scaleLess survives than you expect
    • A hoarding carries one idea and at most seven words. If it needs a second sentence it is a press ad, not a hoarding.
    • Booth back-walls: keep the middle band clear. Furniture, staff and visitors occupy the bottom 1m, and the top 600mm is usually above the sightline. The message lives between.
    • Check the substrate before choosing a colour. Fabric prints duller than vinyl, and backlit material shifts warm. Approve a swatch on the actual material for anything above 3m.
    • Mind the seams and fixings. Large panels arrive in sections. Nothing important may sit on a seam, a pole pocket or an eyelet.
    • Bleed grows with the piece: 25mm for a roll-up, 100mm or the supplier's figure for a wrap.
    Pre-flightRun this before any file leaves
    • Colour mode is CMYK, with no stray RGB or Lab objects, and spot plates named exactly as the printer expects.
    • Total ink coverage is within the limit for the stock.
    • Images are at the resolution for the final size, not the placed size, and are not upscaled.
    • Fonts are embedded or outlined. Check the PDF's font list rather than assuming.
    • Bleed is present on every edge, with crop marks and a 3mm offset.
    • Nothing critical sits outside the safety margin, or across a fold, gutter or seam.
    • Blacks are built correctly: K100 for text, rich black for large areas.
    • Overprint is set deliberately, not left at the application default.
    • The proof has been seen on the actual stock, and someone has signed it.
    08

    Page Templates.

    For developers, page builders and the integrator

    Chapters 03 and 04 catalogue parts. This chapter catalogues whole pages: the template families the portal actually ships, what varies per tenant, and what must never be forked. One template renders many pages, so a fix here reaches every page in the family in the same session.

    01

    The families

    Every shipped template, and what varies inside it

    A template family is a chassis plus a set of tenants. The chassis carries chrome, layout, motion and observers. The tenant carries content and one accent colour. Any change to the chassis belongs to every tenant of that family, applied in the same session, or the family has silently forked.

    Template indexSource of truth per family
    FamilyRendersPrefixSource
    Design PillarEvery /design vertical and collection landing.dp-*design-architecture.html
    Industry Voices/voices, /voices/search, /voices/{slug}.vx-*voices.html
    Brand Profile/brands/{slug}, three variants.bpr-*brand-profile*.html
    Person Profile/people/{slug}.bpr-*, .pe-*person-profile-*.html
    Directory/brands, /people and their search pages.br-* / .pe-*brands.html, people.html
    Article/design/{slug}, /voices/{slug} bodies.art-*design-article.html
    Featured slotIn Focus, on both directories.if-*brands.html
    Chassis versus tenantThe line that decides who owns a change
    • Chassis: section order, grid, breakpoints, nav and sub-nav, scrollspy, carousel wiring, reveal observers, empty states, every shared class. Fixing one tenant's chassis bug means fixing every tenant's.
    • Tenant: copy, images, logo, the accent hex, and which optional sections are present. Nothing else.
    • Bespoke per-brand pages are rejected. The default answer for a new brand is the same template with a different --brand value. A hand-built page for one client cannot receive a family fix and becomes dead weight the day it ships.
    • Scrollspy arrays and sub-nav hrefs are chassis. When a section id is renamed, both move in the same edit or the sub-nav quietly points at nothing.
    Page template

    Design Pillar (.dp-*), tag-landing template.

    One template renders every Design vertical pillar (Series, Architecture, Interiors, Spaces, Designers, Vastu, Guides) and every Collection landing. Live example: /design/architecture. Source: design-architecture.html. Programmer hooks (PILLAR_NAME, PILLAR_SLUG, COUNT, FILTER_CHIPS, CARDS, SERIES_RAIL) are documented in docs/DESIGN-PILLAR-HANDOFF.md.

    • dp-hero, Crumbs · H1 (Gazpacho 88px) · count chip · one-line dek. No image, type carries the moment. Safe for any pillar name length.
    • dp-filterstrip, Horizontal chip row scoped to the pillar (cities / materials / series sub-tags). Sticky below the subnav so filtering stays available while scrolling the grid.
    • dp-grid, 3-col → 2-col tablet → 1-col mobile. Cards reuse the .hr-card--ed chassis (editorial card, 4:3 thumb on top, white body below).
    • dp-loadmore, Single text-link CTA at the foot of the grid. No faux pagination.
    • dp-series, Related-series rail at the bottom, reusing the shared .rail-outer / .rail carousel chassis. Drag on desktop, native swipe on touch.
    • dp-adslot / dp-adslot__badge, Native "Sponsored" billboard (media left, brand-colored copy panel right, top-left Sponsored badge overlaid on the image).     Page template

    Industry Voices (.vx-*), claim-led card family.

    Three pages: /voices (landing), /voices/search (browse), /voices/{slug} (piece). Sources: voices.html, voices-search.html, voices-article.html. CSS lives in styles.css (search VOICES CHASSIS). Full contract in docs/VOICES-HANDOFF.md.

    Why a new card family at all. Every layout FUNCTION here is reused (grids, rails via initCarousel, section heads, buttons, tokens, the whole .br-* finder, the whole art-* block catalog). What is new is the card FACE, because the Design card design is wrong for this content. /design cards are image-led, the photograph is the story. /voices cards are claim-led, the sentence is the story, the face is the credential, the source is the proof. Reusing .nr-card would have dragged the wrong design layer along with the right function layer.

    • vx-hero, The landing hero, full viewport (100svh minus the nav stack, minus the 64px bottom bar on mobile). Two blocks, kept separate on purpose: .vx-hero__intro is the PAGE (h1 + description, the SEO surface, static per vertical) and .vx-hero__card is the FEATURED PIECE (rotates). Do not let the piece's copy bleed into the intro, or the page appears to be described by whatever story happens to be leading that week.
    • Card anatomy, .vx-hero__card (white, bordered) holds three children in order: the kicker (THIS WEEK · DEVELOPER DIALOGUES, centred, labelling the piece before the quote it labels), the stage (warm inset holding the ink quote box and the speaker), and the foot (.vx-hero__foot: provenance left, read link right, justified on one line). Same three-surface construction as the homepage Voices card, .vc4-card > .vc4-stage > .vc4-bubble.
    • Quote length: four size tiers. A hero quote is editor-supplied and unpredictable. data-len on the blockquote selects a tier (s ≤80 chars, m ≤140, l ≤210, xl beyond), which the template sets server-side with an inline script recomputing it from the real text as a fallback. All four verified to hold the hero at an exact 754px viewport fit. No truncation, ever: no line-clamp, no ellipsis. Cutting a sentence short misrepresents what a named person said, which is the one thing this vertical cannot do. Past the longest tier the hero grows taller than the viewport, which is the honest failure mode; the fix is editorial, not CSS.
    • Below 744px the box is dropped entirely. Card and stage both lose their background, border, radius and padding, and the content lays out directly on the body. Nested surfaces cost real width on a phone: --pad-h 24 + card 14 + stage 14 was 52px of inset per side on a 390px screen, leaving the bubble at 276px and wrapping the speaker's role onto two lines. Dropping the box takes the bubble to the full 332px. The quote mark hides with it (it needed the frame to read as a mark rather than a stray glyph), the intro takes a bottom rule since the card edge no longer separates it, and the foot stacks with order putting the action above the fine print.
    • vx-source, The signature. Hairline rule + SOURCE small-caps + platform and date + outbound link. Repeats on every surface that carries a claim. A quote without a live source is aggregation; a quote with one is intelligence, so the source is shown rather than buried.
    • vx-speaker, Face + name + role. One component, three sizes (--sm 34px, base 44px, --lg 64px). Portraits use object-position:50% 22% for head-safe cropping.
    • vx-card, Our own conversation or perspective. No card media. Order is eyebrow → claim (Gazpacho, leads) → hairline → speaker credit → format. An earlier cut carried a 4:3 portrait on top, which put the same face on the card twice (once as media, once in the credit row) and made the card about the person. The card is about the argument; the person gains standing because the argument is worth reading, so the claim takes the space the image used to. Do not reintroduce .vx-card__media.
    • vx-quote, Curated from elsewhere. Deliberately text-led with no media: we do not own imagery of that person in that moment. Mark, quote, editorial framing line (.vx-quote__why, never optional), small speaker row, source receipt.
    • vx-sp, The Speakers index. Face, current claim, and their appearances across the portal, each name resolving to /people/{slug}.
    • vx-contribute / vx-door, The supply side. Two intake doors (write a perspective, nominate a voice). An opinion vertical with no commissioning budget is fed by recruitment, not by editorial alone.

    Reused without modification: .subnav (Voices vocabulary), .dp-subnav (series tabs), .dp-strip__head, .dp-adslot, .dp-partner, .rail-outer/.rail + initCarousel, .dc-paginator, .subscribe, .btn/.btn-accent/.btn-primary/.btn-link, and on the browse page the entire .br-search-wrap/.br-pill/.br-cdd/.brs-fmodal/.brs-toolbar/.brs-empty finder including its JS. On the piece page the whole art-* block catalog, with .art-qa as the default body block.

    Two byline models, one template. On a Conversation, .art-byline is the Ghar.tv journalist and .art-speaker-strip is the subject. On a Perspective they collapse into one because the speaker wrote it. Conflating them is how a competitor ends up with an "Expert Opinion" section bylined to its own newsroom.

    Quote permalink rule. A captured quote is a card on /voices and in browse. It earns its own /voices/{slug} only once it has editorial framing and a response piece attached. Below that bar it has no URL. A wall of one-sentence pages is thin content and reads as scraping.

    Brand-profile pattern

    Image fallbacks, Intelligence SVG glyph & team monogram tile.

    Two fallback slots on every brand-profile: (1) the Intelligence sub-group when the source article has no OG image, (2) any team-member card when a real portrait doesn't exist. Both are shipped in brand-profile-service.html and brand-profile-teearch.html. Physical (brand-profile.html) and premium (brand-microsite-premium.html) templates should adopt the same variants.

Add bpr-mcard__media--gfx to the media slot and inline the matching category SVG. Same look as the homepage .intl4-card-gfx rail: warm-white canvas, centered glyph. Category = the article's parent (Reports / Market / Infrastructure / Rankings / Analysis / Investment / Legal). SVGs are copy-paste from index.html:2724-2878 (7 blocks in the .intl4-track).
