CSS shipped in brand-profile-service.html and brand-profile-teearch.html; add the same variant blocks to brand-profile.html and brand-microsite-premium.html before using them there.

    Pattern 3, Section registry (brand + person canonical sections)

    Every profile page renders a subset of these sections, in an order picked by the tenant's category composition rules. Canonical section IDs are the URL anchors. Load-bearing: section ID #about is canonical (was #story on developer family, normalised 2026-08-31); section ID #work is canonical (was #projects on developer family). Both retained via data-previous-anchors for URL redirect layer.

    Brand sections (17): hero · about · work · recognition · team · timeline · presence · spotlight · intelligence · voices · products · clients · film · contact. Person sections (12): hero · facts · about · specialises · work · voices · published · recognition · credentials · related · contact · closer.

    Every section has 1–4 variants (e.g. hero.classic / hero.split / hero.ambient / hero.film). Full registry with fields + content-availability rules + entitlement gates lives in docs/PROFILE-SECTIONS-SPEC.json. Composition rules per category live in docs/COMPOSITION-RULES.md. Related: docs/BRAND-ENGINE-ARCHITECTURE.md §3.

    Pattern 4, Section modifier vocabulary (stackable classes)

    Modifiers stack on any section. Not primary variants; cross-cutting attributes. Each modifier is a CSS class suffix.

    --tight, reduced vertical padding. Currently on developer-family #recognition, #timeline, #presence. When a section belongs visually close to its neighbours.

    --attached, removes top boundary; visually links to prior section. Currently on developer-family #recognition attached to #about.

    --minor, de-prioritised visual weight. Smaller title, tighter spacing. Currently on person profile #team (co-workers under contact).

    --dark, dark panel treatment. Currently on .bpr-contact--dark for the moody contact panel variant.

    --seamless-wrap, removes section boundary; flows into next section. Currently on .bpr-about--seamless-wrap.

    Rule: modifiers are for CROSS-CUTTING attributes (spacing, panel colour, priority). If it changes the section's structural shape or content, it's a VARIANT not a modifier. See PROFILE-SECTIONS-SPEC.json § modifiers.

    Pattern 5, Motion profiles (page-level + section-level)

    Four profiles. Pick one at page level via <main data-motion-profile="…">. Any section can override via <section data-motion-profile="…">. Element reveals via [data-reveal] observed by window.gharProfileMotion.

    minimal, opacity fade only, no transform. For financial institutions, technical brands, research-heavy people. Duration --motion-duration-fast (.35s).

    editorial, rise (translateY 20 → 0) per-item, no cascade. Default. For architects, design brands, magazine-style pages. Duration --motion-duration-base (.6s).

    cinematic, rise + scale, GSAP scrub on key stages. For developer brands, luxury tenants (Godrej / Scarlet). Duration --motion-duration-slow (1.2s). GSAP loaded on-demand.

    dynamic, print (opacity + skew) on cards, fade on text. For product brands (Materials / Furniture / Lighting). Duration --motion-duration-base (.6s).

    Recipe from recent Horizon Architects tuning: IntersectionObserver with threshold: 0 + rootMargin: '0px 0px -160px 0px' + per-item observation (no cascade groups). Fires when block is 160px inside viewport. See docs/MOTION-SYSTEM.md.

    All profiles respect @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), no motion visible.

    Pattern 6, Composition rules (which sections light up per category)

    Every category (developer / architect / materials / furniture / lighting / finance / proptech / vastu / interior) has explicit rules for which sections render, in what order, at what priority (required / preferred / optional / premium / fallback / irrelevant), with what default variant.

    Developer (Godrej, Avirahi): hero.classic → about → work.grid → recognition.strip → team.founder → timeline → presence.city_cards → intelligence.title_card → voices → spotlight → film → contact.dark

    Architect (Horizon, TEEARCH): hero.ambient → about.seamless → work.editorial → team.leadership → recognition → clients → presence → voices → spotlight → intelligence → film → contact.light

    Materials (Saint-Gobain, Asian Paints): hero → about → products.catalog → clients.logo_wall → work → team → presence → voices → spotlight → contact

    Furniture (Scarlet, Obeetee): hero.split → about → products.collection → team → work → presence → voices → clients → recognition → contact

    Finance: hero → about → products.featured → presence.city_cards → recognition → voices → intelligence.report_list → contact.dark, all sections on motion.minimal.

    Full tables (including person profile disciplines: architects / interiors / developers / brandleaders / advisors / research) in docs/COMPOSITION-RULES.md. Per-tenant admin overrides via profile_section_configs table, see docs/ADMIN-CONTROLS-SCHEMA.md.

    Pattern 7, Entitlement gates (packages control capabilities, not markup)

    Sections + variants + distribution slots gate on capability keys. Nowhere in code: if (brand.package === 'spotlight'). Everywhere: if (entitlements.has('enhanced_profile')). Packages are bundles of capabilities.

    Section-gated capabilities: enhanced_profile, custom_hero_ambient, commissioned_film, premium_theme, motion_cinematic, person_profile_enhanced, intelligence_integration

    Distribution-gated capabilities: category_priority, homepage_placement, newsletter_distribution, premium_distribution, editorial_recommendation, search_priority

    Content-production capabilities: sponsored_story, ghartalks_appearance, videoworks_short, videoworks_long, voices_curation, creator_campaign, event_sponsorship

    Full capability vocabulary + package bundles + admin overrides in docs/ENTITLEMENTS.md. Capability × package matrix in docs/BRAND-CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md.

    Pattern 8, Entity relationships (Brand ↔ Person ↔ Project)

    The load-bearing gap the Brand Engine closes. Current DB has people.brand_id INT FK NULL, one person → at most one brand. Reality is many-to-many.

    New join tables: brand_person_relationships (role · relationship_type · is_founder · is_leadership · is_featured · display_order · start_date · end_date · visibility) · brand_project_relationships (role: developer / architect / pmc / interior / material_supplier / consultant) · person_project_relationships (role · is_lead).

    Also: person_aliases (maiden_name / initials / handle, supports "Suman Kanodia" ↔ "Suman Bajoria" resolution) · article_entity_mentions (article_id / entity_type / entity_id / mention_kind, normalises attribution).

    Migration is additive. people.brand_id becomes derived (mirrors current primary relationship) until deprecation. Full schema + resolver signatures + resolution rules in docs/ENTITY-RELATIONSHIPS.md.

    Pattern 9, Distribution surfaces (entity cards outside their own profile)

    Every place an entity card appears OTHER than its own profile. Editors never manually place entity cards. One resolver, resolveEntitiesForSurface(surfaceId, context), powers every card.

    Directories: brand_directory · person_directory

    Profile cross-refs: brand_page_related_brands · brand_page_similar_brands · person_page_also_at_brand · person_page_similar_discipline

    Project + locality: project_page_brands_involved · project_page_people_involved · locality_page_professionals · locality_page_developers

    Article surfaces: article_page_recirculation_by_entity · article_page_sponsor_brand_card (auto-injected, see EDITOR-blocks-spec.json autoInjection.rules)

    Homepage + newsletter + search: homepage_brand_carousel · homepage_person_carousel · newsletter_brand_spotlight · search_results_brand_row · search_results_person_row

    Every surface has organic slots (relationship-driven, free) + promoted slots (package-gated). Admin controls: pin / suppress / priority_override. Full registry with ranking vocabulary in docs/DISTRIBUTION-SURFACES.json.

    Featured slot · /brands + /people

    In Focus block .if-block

    Replaces the earlier .sp-block + .dp-adslot combo, which read as a horizontal ad banner. Two kinds (Brand and Person) share the chassis, colours, CTA and rotator host. Colour theming rides --brand-canvas and --brand-text, the same tokens the .dp-adslot family uses. Mobile is deliberately not a scaled-down desktop for either kind.

    This block sizes off its container, not the viewport. .if-block sets container-type: inline-size, so the composition answers to the width it is actually given. Use the control below to see all three: under 760px it is a lead photo with an identity card over the fade, from 760px it drops the photo for a three-tile work strip, and from 880px the Person kind gains its third column.

    The block ships as <aside class="if-block sp-block"> inside .sp-rotator. Both classes are required: .if-block is the composition and the container, .sp-block is what the rotator shows and hides. Set the tenant hex on .if-block__inner through inline --brand-canvas and --brand-text. Person cards also set --brand-soft, used by the monogram-portrait fallback.

    Colour-family rule. The dominant right-edge tone of the lead photo, and the bottom tone of each work tile, must sit in the same family as --brand-canvas, or the fade shows a seam and the block reads as two halves stapled together. Verify any replacement image against that before swapping.

    02

    Brand profile (.bpr-*)

    One chassis, three variants, one accent per tenant

    Every /brands/{slug} page is the same template with a different accent hex. Three variants exist because the businesses differ in what they can show: a physical-product brand has product photography, a service practice has projects and people, a premium tenant buys extra surfaces. The chassis is identical across all three.

    Accent colourSourced from the tenant, constrained by us
    • The accent is the brand's real colour, taken from their own logo or site. Never a Ghar.tv theme token. Picking Terracotta for a brand whose identity is navy misrepresents them, so the backend stores the tenant's actual hex.
    • Its surface area is tiny. Eyebrow underline, active thumbnail, CTA fill, hover state. Never a section background, never a large block. Roughly 95% of the page stays neutral warm-white with ink type, which is what lets the page survive a garish or low-contrast tenant hex.
    • A "sand" surface mood was tried and rejected outright. Warm-white or a genuinely dark canvas are the only surface options on these pages.
    • No canonical shapes on tenant pages. Shapes are Ghar.tv's mark, and putting them on someone else's profile confuses whose identity is on screen.
    • No font swaps, no layout swaps. One template, one type system. A Linktree-style per-tenant restyle is not on offer.
    ⚠
    Open risk Free-form accent entry by a backend editor. Editors uploading content rarely have design training, and a garish or low-contrast hex can wreck a page if it is ever allowed to paint a large surface. The constraint above is the only thing holding this; a validated swatch picker is the real fix.
    Logo tilesTwo hard rules, both learned the expensive way
    PropertyValueWhy
    Tile backgroundWhite for a dark or coloured logo, dark grey or black for a light oneNever the brand's own hex. An Asian Paints red logo on an Asian Paints red panel is an unreadable blob
    Tile widthwidth: fit-contentThe tile shrink-wraps to whatever the logo needs
    Tile paddingConstant, e.g. 16px 24px desktop, 14px 20px mobileThe padding is the inner gutter, so it must not vary per brand
    Tile min-heightA floor for visual weightStops a short wordmark from reading as an afterthought
    Tile max-widthAn extreme-case capA very wide wordmark cannot break the layout
    Imageheight fixed, width:auto, max-width:100%, object-fit:containA fixed image height gives every brand the same visual weight; the tile expands sideways to accommodate
    • Fixed tile plus capped image is the bug. Fixed height, fixed width, max-width on the image and max-height on the image, together, silently shrink a wide short logo into a corner of the tile.
    • A padded asset is a data bug, not a CSS bug. Some brand PNGs ship with intrinsic transparent padding. Measured: obeetee 96% vertical fill, saint-gobain 97%, asian-paints 86%, godrej-properties 20%, which is 80% whitespace inside the file. Fix the asset by trimming the transparent border and re-exporting with a consistent gutter. Never inflate the CSS tile to compensate, or every well-cropped logo is oversized to cover one bad one.
    • Detect a padded asset fast: draw it to a canvas, scan the alpha channel for the content bounding box, and compare against the natural dimensions. Below roughly 80% fill in either axis, re-export.
    • Brand wordmarks never change on hover. They are identity anchors, not buttons.
    Team photographyReal face or monogram, nothing in between
    PropertyValue
    Aspect4:3 landscape, cropped before upload
    Face positionUpper-centre third, never within 5% of the top edge
    FramingShoulders-up to chest-up. Avoid full body unless the tile is deliberately larger
    ResolutionMinimum 600 × 450, ideally 800 × 600
    FormatJPEG at 85 to 90% quality
    Runtime safety netobject-fit:cover; object-position:center 15%; plus a --brand-soft background
    • Pre-crop, always. Runtime object-position biasing works for a standard headshot and fails on a portrait source forced into a landscape tile, a group photo, an off-centre subject or a full-body shot. It is a safety net, not the fix.
    • 4:3 landscape, not portrait. A portrait tile made cards too tall in a desktop three-column grid.
    • The photo is the real face of the named person, or it is a Gazpacho monogram tile. Never a stock face, never an AI face, never a different employee.
    Both failure modes, with the real filesSame tile rules, different assets

    Left column is the CSS bug: a fixed box with a capped image. Right column is the pattern: constant padding, fixed image height, tile shrink-wrapped. The bottom row swaps in godrej-properties.original-padded.png, the untrimmed file measured at 20% vertical fill, to show that a correct tile cannot rescue a padded asset.

    Fixed tile, capped image

    A wide mark shrinks to fit the height; a padded file shrinks twice.

    fit-content tile, fixed image height

    Top mark now reads at full weight. Bottom one still does not: that is the asset, and it needs re-exporting.

    Accent surface areaThe same tenant hex, two amounts of it

    Identical content, identical colour #c67e35. On the left it is the canvas. On the right it is a 34px keyline. The left is what the In Focus block used to be, and it is why it read as bought space on a warm-white page rather than as part of the publication.

    03

    Directories and person profiles

    /brands, /people, their search pages, and /people/{slug}

    /people mirrors the /brands shell with a .br- to .pe- prefix swap and the canonical .bpr-person card. They are two verticals, not one Community master. Both search pages share the same finder, the same city matcher and the same reveal helper.

    Search results pageThe header is a result title, not a page title

    Nobody lands on a search page cold. The entrances are the finder, the nav search, or a shared result URL, so by render time the visitor has already expressed a query. The H1 says that query back, assembled from the same category, sub-category, city and free-text values the cards were just filtered on, so heading and grid can never disagree. It also sets document.title.

    StateH1
    Nothing selectedPeople across India
    CategoryArchitects across India
    Category and cityArchitects in Mumbai
    City onlyPeople in Mumbai
    Sub-categoryArchitects · {sub} across India
    Free textResults for “motta”
    • The title shows only what was searched. A filter the reader did not set is not named in the heading.
    • One paid surface per page. The imageless hero and the featured-person card are the same inventory; both do not run together.
    • Category first, then city. City does not discriminate here: roughly half of /brands is multi-city and both directories are Mumbai-heavy. Category cuts the set to a browsable slice and matches how readers arrive. The flex:1.55 against flex:1 split on the finder pill already encodes that hierarchy.
    No person without a portraitA portal rule, not a preference
    • A directory whose job is "who is this person" does not do that job for an entry with no face. Monogram entries at scale made the grid look unfinished.
    • Hide, never delete. The taxonomy (discipline, city, tags, slug, role) is the expensive part. Add is-no-portrait to the card, and restoring a person is one class removal plus an image source.
    • Wire the hidden class into every count, or the page lies. On /people that meant two places: window.gharGridReveal(), which batches whole rows off the live card count and would otherwise leave holes, and the finder's result counter, which would have reported hits above an empty grid.
    /people/{slug} is a personal portfolioThe mistake to never repeat

    A version of this page was assembled out of brand-microsite parts: .bpr-topbar chrome, .bpr-mcard media rails, tinted .bpr-intel-card tiles, the .bpr-contact tenant band. It came out reading as a company page with someone's face at the top. Brand-microsite parts carry a company's body language; a person's page needs the opposite. Build the sections for a person, even when that means writing new CSS instead of reusing a rail.

    • The hero carries only the four universal fields. No verified badge.
    • Work renders in three modes depending on what the record holds.
    • Published work is a lead item plus a list, not a grid of thumbnails.
    • The second half of the same mistake is letting "never fabricate" collapse into shipping almost nothing. Six real project photographs sat in the record while the page showed three of them at 320px in a carousel. Honesty about missing assets is not a reason to under-use the assets that exist.
    • Generated by scripts/build-person-profiles.mjs. Routes go in both vercel.json and serve.mjs, and serve.mjs needs a restart.
    04

    Paid surfaces

    Where sponsorship may appear, and where it may not
    The placement ruleEditorial surfaces only

    Sponsored, featured and paid attributions appear only on surfaces the reader is consuming. They never appear on functional surfaces the reader is doing: a subscribe form, a sign-in modal, a Post Property CTA, a contact form.

    SurfaceSponsor attributionWhy
    Featured story or hero cardYesThe article is editorial content; a partnership strip on its own card is a legitimate publisher relationship
    In-stream sponsored articleYesA native item in the feed with a Sponsored pill, reading as one more story
    Dedicated ad slot (.dp-adslot)YesClearly labelled inventory
    Featured brands moduleYesThe tiles are the inventory
    Newsletter subscribe blockNoThe reader is performing an action. "This subscription form is brought to you by X" is a nonsensical relationship and reads as desperate
    Sign-in, Post Property, contact formNoFunctional CTAs must feel neutral and trustworthy. Mixing sales pitch with functional trust breaks both
    Section headers, eyebrows, topic stripsNoSponsorship is per-card. A section-level attribution is only acceptable when the whole strip is a paid takeover
    No ad gate before editorialThe stream leads, paid punctuates

    On any /design landing, no paid surface appears in the first viewport or above the editorial stream. A page that led with a sponsored hero plus a native billboard stacked under a small title hero showed the reader two ads before a single editorial item.

    #Block
    1Hero: breadcrumb, title, dek
    2Chip strip (filter and return path)
    3Editorial stream starts, heading plus at least three real items
    4In-stream sponsored article, reading as one more stream item
    5More editorial items
    6Native billboard at the foot of the stream
    7Featured brands module
    8Newsletter
    9Brand Connect CTA
    • Collection pages skip the chip strip. Chips are a pillar-level filter, and on a collection there is nothing left to filter.
    • A story surfaced in a curated top slot is excluded from every sub-category and franchise strip below it. Otherwise the newest story appears twice and the pillar reads as either a lazy CMS or a thin archive.
    • The two surfaces carry different content roles by design: the curated slot is editorial voice on a slow cadence, the strips are the news cycle. When both hold their role, overlap is rare and the de-duplication rule is only the safety net.
    Spotlight is identity-led, never photo-ledThe structural fix, not a swap

    The paid slot on /brands and /people was once a rail of 4:5 photo cards. That format required a photograph, so a brand with no usable imagery got stock. Two stock images went live against a real client about to sign, and one was the og:image, so every share of that profile previewed a stranger.

    • The block is identity-led: brand colour canvas, the brand's own logo, name, one line, city, CTA. Photography is an optional media column.
    • A brand with no imagery still gets a complete, honest, on-brand block, so nothing tempts anyone to fill a hole with stock.
    • One visible tenant at any N, on a daily rotation, rather than a rail that hides paid placement behind a swipe.
    • The quarantined stock images are kept in brand_assets/_quarantine-stock/ as a record. Do not reuse them.
    09

    Motion.

    For developers and designers

    Timing floors and caps, motion deltas, easing, triggers and fallbacks. Every number here was set by iteration on a real section, usually after something was rejected for feeling cheap or rushed. Start from these values rather than from a guess, and the first version is usually the one that ships.

    01

    Pacing

    Subtle and slow is the default

    Five iterations on one homepage card established these limits. Anything faster read as cheap; anything slower lost the reader before the payoff. Treat the floor as a floor, not a target.

    Per-element timingSeconds
    PhaseFloorSweet spotCap
    Single fade-in (opacity 0 to 1, blur 14 to 0)1.01.3 to 1.62.0
    Full enter-and-exit cycle1.51.7 to 2.02.4
    Stagger between sequential elements0.81.2 to 1.51.8
    Total sequence for a section revealn/a8 to 1112
    Motion deltasHow far anything may move
    PropertyMax safe deltaWhy
    translateY / translateX±12pxMore reads as a swoop. Subtle entries stay under ±8px
    scale0.92 to 1.08, absolute max 1.15Big scales feel jumpy rather than cinematic
    blur0 to 14pxThe proven range for a blur-focus reveal. Past 20px it reads as a glitch
    Colour shift on hoverOne step on the value scaleWarm-white to pure white, never turmeric to terracotta
    EasingTwo curves, and what to avoid
    • Default: ease. Slow start, smooth middle, slow end. Reads as deliberate.
    • One-shot reveals where the end state should anchor: cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), a gentle out-expo.
    • Avoid cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .2, 1) for entries. It feels snappy and slightly bouncy.
    • Never spring, overshoot or bounce on editorial content. It belongs to toys, not to a publication.
    • Only ever animate transform and opacity, plus filter: blur() where the reveal calls for it. Never transition-all.
    Feel the differenceThe same reveal at three paces

    Same four elements, same properties, same stagger structure. Only the numbers change. Play the rushed setting once and the house setting once: the argument for the floor stops being a table and starts being obvious.

    02

    Triggers and fallbacks

    Fire on arrival, degrade to the end state

    A section eleven blocks down the homepage is not on screen at load. Triggering on DOMContentLoaded means the reader misses the animation entirely and arrives at a finished state with no idea anything happened.

    Canonical observerCopy this shape
    // Fires once, when the reader has actually landed on the section.
new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
  entries.forEach(function (e) {
    if (e.isIntersecting && !played) {
      played = true;
      el.classList.add('is-playing');
      io.disconnect();
    }
  });
}, { threshold: 0.5, rootMargin: '-8% 0px -8% 0px' });
    • threshold: 0.5 so at least half the element is on screen. Reveal observers use 0.5; carousel autoplay uses 0.15, because starting a rail early is harmless and starting a story reveal early wastes it.
    • rootMargin: -8% top and bottom, so the element must be genuinely inside the viewport rather than skimming the edge.
    • Disconnect after firing. A reveal plays exactly once per page load. Replaying on every scroll-back is the fastest way to make a page feel cheap.
    • Add is-playing to the section, not to each child. Child animations are CSS keyframes scoped under .is-playing .child, so the JS stays one line and the choreography stays in CSS.
    Two mandatory fallbacksShip them in the same commit as the animation
    /* JS or IntersectionObserver unavailable: show the end state immediately */
.x-stage:not(.is-playing):not(.no-anim) .x-child { /* end-state values */ }

/* Reduced motion: no animation, snap to the end state */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .x-child { animation: none; /* end-state values */ }
}
    • If JS fails, add .no-anim to suppress the default-hidden state. An animation that never fires must not leave content invisible.
    • prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is not optional, and it means no animation, not a faster one.
    • GSAP loads deferred. Anything that must be visible without it needs a CSS end state, not a JS one.
    03

    Hover, and the click target

    The element that receives the click must never move

    Hard rule. Put the lift, scale or rotate on a non-interactive inner element, never on the outer anchor or button. This was found dropping real clicks on a live brand profile.

    The failure modeWhy a 3px lift drops clicks
    • The reader hovers near the bottom edge of a card.
    • transform: translateY(-3px) moves the card up, so the cursor is now over empty space below it.
    • mouseleave fires, the transform reverts, the card comes back under the cursor, mouseenter fires. The cycle repeats as a flicker.
    • A click during the flicker can land mousedown and mouseup on different elements, so click never fires at all.
    • Inside a carousel it is worse: the shifted position reads as intentional motion to the drag detector, and the click is suppressed as a drag.
    /* WRONG: the click target moves on hover */
.card { cursor: pointer; transition: transform .3s; }
.card:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); }

/* RIGHT: an inner element moves, the click target stays put */
.card { cursor: pointer; }
.card__media { transition: transform .3s; }
.card:hover .card__media { transform: translateY(-3px); }
    The universal hover-suppression trapCosts about five rounds of debugging if you do not know it

    A rule like @media (hover: none){ *:hover{ transform:none !important } }, added to stop expensive card hover effects firing during a swipe, will also silently kill the transform of any layout element that briefly enters hover on a touch device. Touch hover sticks until something else is tapped.

    • The symptom is "the JS class is removed but the element does not visually animate out". The off-canvas close button appeared dead: oc-open was correctly removed from both the menu and the overlay, confirmed by a mutation observer, yet computed transform read none instead of translateX(100%). The overlay had no transform, so it faded correctly, making it look like the background closed and the menu stayed.
    • Why specificity does not save you. #ocMenu at 100 beats *:hover at 10, but the !important on the universal rule flips it, because the base rule did not use !important.
    • Fix at the source by excluding layout and animation elements from the universal selector: *:hover:not(#ocMenu):not(#ocOverlay):not(#joinModal).
    • The wrong fix that looks like it works is !important on the animating element's transform. The value override wins, but transition-property: none !important from the universal rule still applies as the hover state ticks, producing a stuttery slide. It passes a screenshot and fails in motion. Always exclude at the source.
    • Diagnose the cascade before adding defensive JS. Five rounds went into event-layer theories (pointer-events, capture-phase handlers, reloads) when the bug was one CSS override. If JS state is right and the visual is wrong on touch, and the element positions itself with transform, check this rule first.
    Hover vocabularyWhat a state change may use
    • Cards: border-colour shift, layered shadow deepening, a translate on an inner element. Never a background gradient painted onto the surface.
    • Text-link CTAs: motion only. gap widens from 6px to 9px and the arrow translates 2px on X. The colour stays var(--ink). Red is a brand anchor at roughly 5% of a page, and it stops being one if every card hover flashes it.
    • Brand wordmarks: no hover change at all.
    • :focus-visible may use brand red. Focus is a different affordance from hover.
    Reproduce itHover the lower edge of each card, then click

    Both cards are links to the same place. The only difference is which element carries the hover transform. Move the pointer slowly onto the bottom edge of each: the left one starts flickering, because it moves out from under the cursor, fires mouseleave, falls back, and fires mouseenter again. Then try to click while it flickers.

    Transform on the anchor

    Hover my bottom edge

    enter/leave cycles 0 · clicks landed 0

    Transform on the media

    Hover my bottom edge

    enter/leave cycles 0 · clicks landed 0

    The cycle counter is the tell. On the right it goes up by one per approach, because the anchor never moves. On the left it climbs as long as you hold the edge, and every cycle is a chance for mousedown and mouseup to land on different elements, which produces no click at all.

    04

    Carousel motion

    Where JS owns the scroll
    Scroll-snap fights the animationThe jagged-drag bug

    With scroll-snap-type: x mandatory, the browser re-snaps to the nearest snap point on every scrollLeft mutation, including the per-frame mutations from a rAF loop. A 1200px animation that should produce roughly 44 smooth scroll events instead produces four chunky 300px jumps, because the browser is yanking to snap points behind you. Separately, scroll-behavior: smooth turns any post-animation snap correction into its own animated scroll, which is the visible stutter at the end.

    • When JS owns snapping, set scroll-snap-type: none, or proximity if lenient wheel snap is wanted. Never mandatory.
    • Set scroll-behavior: auto. Paginator and autoplay can still pass behavior:'smooth' explicitly to scrollBy or scrollTo.
    • During a drag, force both again through an .is-dragging class with !important, in case a base rule overrides.
    Hover shadows must never be guillotinedPad the track on all four sides

    A horizontal overflow-x: auto container is a scroll container in both axes as far as painting is concerned: the browser forces overflow-y: visible to auto, which hard-clips shadow ink at the padding box on all four sides. Padding the bottom alone fixes the drop shadow and still guillotines the first card's left shadow and the last card's right.

    • Pad the track on every side, scaled to the shadow's projection: padding: 12px 24px 40px 24px suits a 0 30px 60px -28px shadow.
    • Compensate with matching negative margins on the wrapper so the cards still fill the container and the section rhythm is unchanged.
    • With snap scrolling, mirror the padding in scroll-padding so snap targets align to the shadow-clearance area.
    • At section level use overflow-x: clip; overflow-y: visible, never overflow: hidden. clip does not force the other axis, which is exactly why it is the right keyword here.
    • QA by hovering the first, middle and last card, in scrolled state, and confirming a soft halo on all four sides.
    Bleed or contained, never bothThe rail-slicing bug
    VariantOuter marginSection overflowClipped by
    Bleed (portal default)margin-inline: calc(-1 * var(--pad-h))none at allbody's global overflow-x: clip
    Containedzerooverflow-x: clip; overflow-y: visiblethe section content edge
    • Mixing them cancels out. A bleed margin plus a clip on the same box makes the rail bleed to the --max-w edge and then cut at exactly that line. Because --max-w is clamp(1280px, 75vw, 1840px), on a 1440px screen the cut lands about 75px inside the viewport, slicing cards with a hard vertical edge and a dead gutter beyond.
    • To diagnose: walk up from the .rail-outer to the first ancestor whose computed overflow-x is not visible. On a healthy bleed rail that ancestor is body, and its right edge equals the layout viewport width. Anything else means the rail is being cut early.
    See the guillotineHover the first and last tile in each track

    Two identical tracks, identical tiles, identical hover shadow. The top one has no clearance inside its scroll container, so the shadow is cut at the padding box on all four sides. Hover the first tile and watch its left shadow disappear at the edge; the bottom track pads all four sides and pulls the padding back with negative margins, so the halo renders whole.

    What does not count as subtle

    All of these were built, shown and rejected
    • Slot-machine cycling under one second per cycle. Reads as a glitching carousel, not as motion.
    • Push animations where elements shove each other around the screen.
    • A wordmark scaling from zero to natural size on entry. That is a logo intro, and this is a page.
    • Several simultaneous animations with overlapping start times. Chaotic at any duration.
    • Letterbox bars sliding in for cinematic feel on a homepage card. Over-stylised.
    • Animating border-radius from 0 to 20px. Reads as a rendering artifact, not as a transition.
    • Animating an ambient loop with opacity instead of motion. For a continuous ambient graphic, animate position and use a stack-drop translate with a step-end swap. Cap stacking layers at three, run entry and exit in the same order, keep the cycle at 20 seconds or longer, and let the entry settle before the ambient starts.
    ⚠
    Authoritative elsewhere Brand Service Template SVG animation has its own spec at docs/BRAND-SERVICE-TEMPLATE-ANIMATION-SPEC.md, including byte caps (hero under 150KB preferred, 250KB maximum; About under 100KB preferred, 150KB maximum), the mandatory <title> and <desc>, and the reduced-motion reset. Read that document before generating one, rather than working from this chapter.
    10

    Engineering Contract.

    For developers and the integrator

    Where files live, what loads in what order, which helpers already exist, and the cascade traps that have cost real debugging time on this codebase. Read this before writing a helper: the commonest defect in this repo is a second implementation of something that already ships.

    01

    Reuse first

    The protocol, before any new markup, CSS or JS

    Ghar.tv is a portal: many pages, one design language. Every fork (a second rail chassis, a second chip, a second arrow button) is a future bug surface and something a human has to reconcile at integration. Run this before writing anything, every time.

    Four stepsIn this order
    • 1. Search the existing assets. This catalog first, then styles.css by visual or role keyword (chip, rail, card, arrow, fade), then main.js, ghar-carousel.js and ghar-ticker.js for a function that already does it.
    • 2. Split the need into design and function. They come from different places and can be reused independently. If an existing chassis has the function you need but its design is wrong for your context, reuse the function only and keep the local design. Do not drag both layers along.
    • 3. Never paper over a wrong-context default with override CSS. If a chassis fits 80% but its assumptions do not apply (grid bleed inside a modal, breakpoint-gated visibility, hover-only arrows), that is the signal to reuse the function only, not to stack overrides.
    • 4. If something genuinely new is needed, add it here as a catalog entry, so the next page reuses it instead of inventing a third version.
    A worked example of step 2Why /voices got a new card face

    Every layout function on /voices is reused: grids, rails through initCarousel, section heads, buttons, tokens, the whole .br-* finder, the whole art-* block catalog. What is new is the card face, because /design cards are image-led (the photograph is the story) and /voices cards are claim-led (the sentence is the story, the face is the credential, the source is the proof). Reusing .nr-card would have dragged the wrong design layer along with the right function layer. That is the distinction step 2 is asking for.

    02

    Files and load order

    The root is production only
    Where a file goesDecide before saving, not after

    The root holds shipped pages, the CSS and JS they load, build config, and asset folders. If you cannot point at a route for a page in vercel.json, serve.mjs, sitemap.xml or a link in partials/, it is not a production file and it does not belong in the root.

    DirectoryWhat it holds
    _dev/prototypes/Test pages, previews, option and variant explorations
    _dev/archive/Superseded versions and pre-edit backups
    _dev/reference/Read but never shipped: this catalog, reports, decks
    _dev/templates/Templates a build script reads or writes
    _dev/tools/One-off scripts: scrapers, screenshot runners, audits, codemods
    _dev/scratch/Throwaway text and JSON dumps
    • _dev/ is a single .gitignore rule, so a new prototype needs no ignore edit and can never leak into the deploy by accident.
    • serve.mjs maps every .html under _dev/*/ at boot and falls back to it on a root 404, so a moved page keeps its original URL. Always open the short root URL: these files use relative asset paths that only resolve from the root.
    • A genuinely new production page needs its route added in the same commit, in both vercel.json and serve.mjs. serve.mjs needs a restart to pick it up.
    Head order for a standalone pageGet this wrong and the type silently falls back

    dist/styles.min.css references font-family:'Inter' everywhere but never declares the @font-face. Inter is self-hosted from fonts/inter-var.woff2, and the declarations live inline in each page's head, deliberately, to avoid a two-request waterfall. A page that omits them falls back to San Francisco or Segoe UI. Readers notice that the type looks off without being able to say why.

    #TagNote
    1<link rel="preload" as="font"> for inter-var.woff2crossorigin required
    2Inline <style> with three @font-face blocksLatin, Latin-extended, and the italic variable face. Without the italic file the browser skews the upright, which looks bad on Inter
    3gazpacho.cssDisplay face
    4dist/styles.min.css?v=NShared chassis
    5The page's own <style>Loads last, so at equal specificity it wins. See the next section
    • To confirm at runtime: document.fonts.check('400 16px Inter') in the console.
    • nav.css is served raw with a ?v=N cache-buster on 17 pages. Bump it in the same commit as any nav.css change.
    03

    Cascade traps

    Four bugs that look like broken JS
    Shared CSS loses to a page style blockHit three times in one session

    Every page links dist/styles.min.css and then declares its own <style> after it. Two class selectors are both specificity (0,1,0), so source order decides and the page always wins. A "must not render" utility living in styles.css therefore needs !important, or it silently loses. The failure is invisible in review: the rule looks right, the JS that adds the class runs correctly, nothing errors, and the element simply never hides.

    UtilityBeaten byFix
    .is-spotlight-dupe{display:none}.brand-card{display:flex}!important
    .pe-empty[hidden].pe-empty{display:flex}!important
    .br-cdd__sub--all.br-cdd__sub declared laterMove the block after its sibling
    • Proving the JS found the right element is not proof the element hides. Resolve the actual cascade winner: read both stylesheets in link order, find every display declaration that matches, and apply source order plus !important. A match test and a render test are different tests.
    • When a button carries two classes, the modifier block must be declared after the base block. At equal specificity the later one wins, so moving a modifier above its base silently reverts every property.
    Class-name collision with the shared stylesheetFound in this catalog, 2026-09-01

    This page links styles.css so its live demos render exactly as production does. That also means every production class name is in scope here. The catalog's own orientation hero was called .ds-hero, and styles.css already ships a .ds-hero: the Design Stories hero card, with border-radius, overflow:hidden, and a translateY(-3px) hover lift. The doc's hero silently inherited all of it, so a page heading lifted like a card on hover. Renamed to .ds-intro.

    • A prefix is not a namespace. ds- meant "design system doc" here and "design stories" there, and nothing warned about the overlap.
    • Check before you name. grep -o '\.your-class[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]' styles.css takes a second and catches this. The other doc-chrome prefixes on this page were audited at the same time and are clean.
    • The same audit is worth running whenever a new page-local class is added to any page that links the shared stylesheet, which is every page.
    The dangling selector commaA comment is whitespace to the parser

    Commenting out a "redundant" selector inside a multi-selector list, without removing the trailing comma on the line above, silently merges the orphaned selector into the next rule. The parser treats the comment as whitespace, so a hover rule quietly acquires a block of layout properties. The reported symptom was a sudden jump and clipping on card hover, two sections away from the edit.

    • When you comment a selector out of a list, delete the trailing comma on the line above in the same edit.
    • Better: delete the selector rather than commenting it. Version control is the archive.
    Two more in the same familyBoth look like JS bugs
    • display: revert reverts to the user-agent value, not the author value. On a display:flex card it yields block and breaks the layout. To re-show something, remove the hiding class in JS. Never override it in CSS.
    • A :hover rule with a descendant combinator reaches nested elements that a matching > child transition does not. That is why a brand-card logo snapped while the photo behind it eased.
    No spacing-only classesThe fastest way to fork a design system

    Three classes, one role, three slightly different clamp() values, with no functional reason for the variance. If you are about to write a rule whose body is only margin-* or padding-*, stop.

    /* What not to do */
.ad4-pills-outer   { margin-bottom: clamp(28px, 3vw, 40px); }
.intl4-chips-outer { margin-bottom: clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 44px); }
.gev-chips-outer   { margin-top: clamp(28px, 3vw, 36px); margin-bottom: clamp(28px, 3vw, 40px); }

/* What to do: co-class the role-named canonical */
<div class="section-pills-strip">
    • Co-class an existing role-named canonical: .section-block, .section-block--warm, .section-pills-strip, .section-head, .feat-list. Each already carries its own spacing.
    • If no canonical exists for the role, add one to styles.css named by role, pick one standard value, document it here, and co-class it everywhere.
    • Never a per-section prefix for spacing alone.
    04

    Shared chrome is generated

    Never hand-edit inside a PARTIAL block

    Everything between <!-- PARTIAL nav:start --> and <!-- PARTIAL nav:end --> is generated, and the same applies to footer, oc-menu, join-modal, mobile-search-modal, bottom-bar, subscribe, br-contact-modal and br-brief-modal. npm run build:partials overwrites the whole span from partials/<name>.html across every page in the PAGES list in scripts/build-partials.mjs.

    Why this rule existsNothing warns you

    A search button was added straight into one page's .nav-actions. It worked, and it tested clean at every breakpoint. The next build:partials run would have deleted it silently: the build reports "expansion written" and the button is simply gone.

    • A new control in shared chrome goes into partials/<name>.html, then rebuild.
    • Per-page controls ship in the partial for every page and switch on with a body class. That pattern is already there for the two CTAs: .nav-btn--cta{display:none} plus body.cta-subscribe .nav-cta--subscribe.
    • Keep the partial's copy generic (aria-label="Search") and let the owning page specialise at runtime, rather than forking the partial.
    • Behaviour stays with the feature, not in nav.css. A page carrying the class with no handler ships a dead button, so add the class and the handler together.
    • index.html is not on the partial system and does not load nav.css. It keeps its own inline copy of the nav CSS, so any portal-wide nav change has to be made in both places or the homepage silently diverges.
    05

    Shared helpers

    These already exist. Do not write a second one
    HelperOwnsUsed by
    initCarousel()Every horizontal rail: drag, momentum, overflow detection, paginator wiringEvery rail on the portal, without exception
    window.gharCityMatch()City filtering on every directory surface/brands, /people, both search pages
    window.gharGridReveal()Progressive reveal of a directory grid, by whole rows/brands, /people
    window.gharCanCollapseNav()Whether the masthead may hideEvery page with a sub-nav
    gharCityMatchTwo rules a string equality gets wrong
    • A metro selection matches its satellites. Mumbai must find Alibaug, Thane, Navi Mumbai and Borivali. Delhi NCR must find Noida, Gurugram, Ghaziabad and Faridabad. Aliases also cover older names people still type: Bangalore, Madras, Calcutta, Pondicherry.
    • National entries match every city. Roughly half of /brands is multi-city, so equality matching hid most of the inventory the moment a city was picked, which is the opposite of what a filter is for. Kolkata went from 1 result to 14.
    • The national pattern is /multi-?city|pan-?india|nationwide|all india/i, deliberately not a bare india, which would false-positive on a firm name sitting inside the location string.
    • It reads the location text already on the card, so no card needed re-stamping with extra data attributes.
    gharGridRevealRows, never a fixed card count
    window.gharGridReveal({
  grid, sentinel, cardSelector, initialRows, batchRows, holdMs
});
    • A fixed batch of 12 meant three different things per breakpoint: 4 rows at 3-up, 6 at 2-up, 12 at 1-up. It also left a ragged part-row whenever the eligible count was not a multiple of the column count, which now happens constantly as filtered and de-duplicated cards come and go.
    • The helper reads the live column count from computed grid-template-columns, reveals whole rows, and re-multiplies on resize, so the reader keeps their place and never sees a half-filled row. Defaults: 4 initial rows, 3 per batch.
    • The eligible list is recomputed every pass, never captured once, so a changing card count cannot leave a stale cursor. Excluded from counting: de-duplication hides, .is-filtered-out, and the empty state.
    • Exposes grid.__revealAll() so a filter can bypass paging (a filtered result must never be hidden by the loader) and grid.__revealReset() to return to paged browsing when filters clear.
    ⚠
    Load-order trap dist/main.min.js is loaded with defer, so a non-deferred inline script parses before it and any ghar* helper is undefined at that moment. That is why the initial filter call on the search pages is wrapped in the same setTimeout retry the carousels use for initCarousel. Deferred inline scripts are fine, since they run in document order after the bundle.
    06

    Defensive layer for backend content

    Counts, lengths, dimensions and missing fields

    The behaviour requirement is in Chapter 05. This is the implementation: the canonical classes that already ship in styles.css, and the sections that still assume a fixed count.

    Canonical defensive CSSAlready in styles.css
    /* Empty containers collapse (N=0) */
.rail:empty, .dc-track:empty, .grid-3col-editorial:empty,
.feat-list:empty, .section-foot:empty, .dc-paginator:empty { display: none; }

/* Optional backend field */
.collapse-when-empty:empty { display: none; }

/* N=1: a single card must not stretch into a fractional-n slot */
.rail-outer:not(.is-overflowing) .rail > *:only-child { max-width: max-content; }

/* Paginator hides when there is nothing to scroll to */
.rail-outer:not(.is-overflowing) ~ .dc-paginator { display: none; }

/* Hide a "See all" CTA when the trailing rail or grid is empty */
.section-head:has(+ .rail-outer .rail:empty) .section-head__link { display: none; }
    Mapping variance to a classWhat to reach for
    Backend varianceClass
    Optional title that may be missing.collapse-when-empty
    An 80-character title.line-clamp-2 or .line-clamp-3
    A long city or chip label.truncate
    Any dynamic imageWrap in .aspect-4-3 (or the right ratio), .img-cover on the image
    A variable price, count or stat.tabular-nums
    A long byline inside a flex child.flex-shrink-safe
    Empty arrayNo class needed, :empty collapse handles it
    Single-item arrayNo class needed, the :only-child rule handles it
    • Patterns that pass by construction: carousels on .rail-outer plus initCarousel, 1fr columns, and repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)).
    • Patterns that fail: hard-coded column counts such as 1fr 1fr 1fr, aspect-locked images with no wrapper, and a section head with a "See all" link above nothing.
    • A broken-image fallback tint already exists for src values that are empty, undefined or null.
    ⚠
    Known brittle sections These encode an exact item count in their structural CSS, so the universal defensive layer does not save them. Each needs its own refactor to auto-fit or to the carousel chassis before the CMS is wired: Brand Connect three-pillar (.bc4v2-track), ecoForYou four-card hero (.e4-cards), GharEvents three-shape (.ge4-cards), Services three-card (.sv4-cards), the Creator Network four-step journey, and the three-column editorial grid hero. They do not break today because the data is static. They will break the day it is not.
    11

    The Register.

    For everyone, and for any AI tool working on this codebase

    One scannable list of every hard rule in this system, with the reason attached, followed by the debts that are still open. Search this chapter first when you are about to do something and are not sure whether it has already been ruled out. Every line here was written after it went wrong once.

    01

    Never

    Rejected, with the reason, so it is not re-proposed
    Colour and surface
    NeverBecauseInstead
    Brand red on an eyebrow, tag, date, dot, quote mark, border or bulletRed is a brand anchor at roughly 5% of a page. Spending it on decoration retires itvar(--faint) for labels, var(--rule) for structure
    A subtle multi-stop gradient as a card or banner backgroundIt muddies the surface and reads as generic. It was called out in exactly those termsA flat solid, or a committed dark panel
    A gradient as a card hover stateIt competes with the card's own surface and reads as a dirty tintBorder-colour shift, layered shadow, inner-element translate
    A coloured top strip, top border or category tab on a cardEvery section starts reading as a different site. It is the cheap default moveEyebrow text for category, section background for differentiation
    A plain filled dot beside a title, wordmark or eyebrowIt reads as a placeholder bullet and weakens the wordmark it sits next toA real mark: a seal, a monogram, a typographic ornament, a thin rule. Dots are fine inside a badge or status pill
    A "sand" surface mood on a tenant pageTried and rejected outrightWarm-white, or a genuinely dark canvas
    Blending a theme colour into a foundation neutralThe result is muddy. Theme colours blend only with theme coloursSolid theme tones, rotated by meaning
    Default Tailwind palette as a primaryIt is the single clearest tell of an untouched templateThe 16-colour Ghar.tv system
    Type
    NeverBecauseInstead
    Negative letter-spacing on GazpachoThe face is drawn for its own tracking. Tightening it fills the countersDefault tracking at every size
    Gazpacho italicsThere is no true italic; the browser skews the uprightColour or weight contrast for emphasis
    Inter for a number at 14px or largerStats and prices are display moments and read as data entry in InterGazpacho 700
    The same face for headings and bodyIt flattens every hierarchy the page is trying to buildGazpacho display against Inter body
    An em dash, anywhereA standing rule on this projectA comma, a colon, a full stop, or a rewritten sentence
    A dollar sign, "millions", or MM/DDThis is an Indian platform₹, lakhs and crores, DD/MM
    Layout and components
    NeverBecauseInstead
    A second carousel chassisEvery fork is a future bug surface and a divergence someone has to reconcile.rail-outer / .rail plus initCarousel plus .dc-paginator, verbatim
    A bleed margin and a section clip on the same railThey cancel, and the cards are sliced at the --max-w edgePick bleed or contained. See Chapter 09
    A CSS rule whose body is only margins or paddingThree classes, one role, three different values, and the system has forkedCo-class the role-named canonical
    A transform on the element that receives the clickIt drops clicks near the edges and confuses carousel drag detectionTransform an inner, non-interactive element
    transition-allIt animates properties you never intended, including layout onesName the properties
    position: fixed on body to lock scrollIt fights ScrollSmoother and loses the reader's placeBlock wheel and touchmove
    Hiding the masthead with no second-level bar to take the topThe page is left with no chrome at allGate on window.gharCanCollapseNav()
    A shape glyph as a category mark, or beside the logoShapes are design moves, not icons, and the logo is never paired with oneUse the shape as a field, a mask or an icon backdrop
    Canonical shapes on a tenant pageThey are Ghar.tv's mark and confuse whose identity is on screenNothing. The tenant's own material carries the page
    A bespoke page for one brandIt cannot receive a family fix and is dead weight the day it shipsThe same template with a different --brand
    Content and imagery
    NeverBecauseInstead
    A stock or AI face for a named personTwo stock images once went live against a real client, one of them as the og:image, so every share previewed a strangerThe real portrait, or a Gazpacho monogram tile
    Listing a person with no portraitA directory that answers "who is this person" is not answering itHide the card with is-no-portrait, and wire that class into every count
    The brand's own hex behind the brand's own logoAn unreadable blob. Confirmed with a red logo on a red panelWhite tile for a dark logo, dark tile for a light one
    A sponsor attribution on a subscribe form, sign-in, or contact CTAThe reader is performing an action, not consuming content. It reads as desperateEditorial surfaces only
    A paid surface in the first viewport of a content pageTwo ads before a single story is not a publicationThe stream leads; paid punctuates
    Truncating a quoteIt misrepresents what a named person saidAn editorial length cap, enforced before publish
    Fabricated statistics, project names or brand precedentUnverifiable claims are the fastest way to lose an industry audienceReal, non-round, early-stage numbers
    A reference brand's name in user-facing copyThey are internal vocabulary for positioning, nothing moreOriginal, user-first copy
